Following a youth stint at [[RSC Anderlecht|R.S.C. Anderlecht]], the then-champions of Belgium, he made his senior debut with HK Kópavogur. At the end of August 2005, Rúrik signed for [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]], but failed to make an appearance for Charlton's first team. On 10 November 2020, Rúrik announced his retirement from football.{{cite news |author1=Ingvi Þór Sæmundsson |title=Rúrik leggur skóna á hilluna |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20202035571d/rurik-leggur-skona-a-hilluna |access-date=10 November 2020 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=10 November 2020 |language=is}} He appeared on series 14 of the German TV programme ''[[Let's Dance (German TV series)|Let’s Dance]]'' and won the competition. ==International career== In 2011, Rúrik was chosen as part of the [[Iceland national under-21 football team|Iceland U21]] squad to represent Iceland at the [[2011 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship]] in Denmark. The striker was named on the bench for the opening game against [[Belarus national under-21 football team|Belarus]]. In May 2018 he was named in [[Iceland national football team|Iceland]]'s 23-man squad for the [[2018 World Cup]] in Russia.{{cite web |last1=Crawford |first1=Stephen |title=Revealed: Every World Cup 2018 squad - Final 23-man lists |url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/revealed-every-world-cup-2018-squad-23-man-preliminary-lists/oa0atsduflsv1nsf6oqk576rb |website=Goal |accessdate=24 March 2022 |date=4 June 2018}} ==Personal life== Rúrik was a candidate for the centre-right [[Independence Party (Iceland)|Independence Party]] in the [[2016 Icelandic parliamentary election]] and [[2017 Icelandic parliamentary election]].{{Cite news|url=https://en.onefootball.com/politics-horror-films-dentistry-icelands-incredible-stories/|title=Politics, dentistry and horror films: Iceland's incredible stories|date=8 June 2018|work=Onefootball English|access-date=24 July 2018|language=en-GB}} After Iceland's [[2018 FIFA World Cup Group D|2018 FIFA World Cup game]] against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]], Rúrik's [[Instagram]] profile went viral, as his followers increased by 250,000 after the game.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} His follower count was right over one million in June 2018, more than triple the size of Iceland's current population.{{Cite news|url=https://icelandmonitor.mbl.is/news/news/2018/06/24/icelandic_team_s_rurik_now_has_over_a_million_insta/|title=Icelandic team's Rúrik now has over a million Instagram followers|date=24 June 2018|work=Iceland Monitor|access-date=30 August 2018|language=en-GB}} In 2021, Rúrik appeared in the action-comedy film ''[[Cop Secret]]'', directed by [[Hannes Þór Halldórsson]].{{cite news |author1=Stefán Árni Pálsson |title=Fyrsta myndefnið úr Leynilöggunni |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20212097749d |access-date=23 April 2021 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=16 April 2021 |language=Icelandic}} In 2021, he won ''[[Let's Dance (German TV series) season 14|Let's Dance]]'' in Germany with Renata Lusin.{{when?|date=April 2026}} Rúrik appeared in the [[Netflix]] comedy film ''[[Eat Pray Bark]]'', released in 2026.{{cite web |title=Eat Pray Bark - Therapie auf vier Pfoten |trans-title=Eat Pray Bark - Therapy on four paws {{Short description|American basketball player (born 1985)}} {{other people||Nick Young (disambiguation)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=March 2015}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Nick Young | image = Nick Young Lakers.jpg | caption = Young with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2014 | position = [[Shooting guard]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 7 | weight_lb = 210 | league = | team = | number = 1, 11, 0, 6, 34 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1985|6|1}} | birth_place = [[Los Angeles]], California, U.S. | high_school = [[Cleveland High School (Los Angeles)|Grover Cleveland]]
(Los Angeles, California) | college = [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] (2004–2007) | draft_year = 2007 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 16 | draft_team = [[Washington Wizards]] | career_start = 2007 | career_end = 2018 | years1 = {{nbay|2007|start}}–{{nbay|2011|end}} | team1 = [[Washington Wizards]] | years2 = {{nbay|2011|end}} | team2 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years3 = {{nbay|2012|full=y}} | team3 = [[Philadelphia 76ers]] | years4 = {{nbay|2013|start}}–{{nbay|2016|end}} | team4 = [[Los Angeles Lakers]] | years5 = {{nbay|2017|full=y}} | team5 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years6 = {{nbay|2018|start}} | team6 = [[Denver Nuggets]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ({{nbafy|2018}}) * 2× First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]] (2006, 2007) | stats_league = NBA | stat1label = [[Point (basketball)|Points]] | stat1value = 8,194 (11.4 ppg) | stat2label = [[Rebound (basketball)|Rebounds]] | stat2value = 1,427 (2.0 rpg) | stat3label = [[Assist (basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = 687 (1.0 apg) }} '''Nicholas Aaron Young''' (born June 1, 1985), nicknamed "'''Swaggy P'''", is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]] and was a two-time first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] selection in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-10]]. Young was selected by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the first round of the [[2007 NBA draft]] with the 16th overall pick. He won an [[NBA championship]] with the [[Golden State Warriors]] in 2018. ==Early life== Born in Los Angeles, California, Young played for Hamilton High School, [[Susan Miller Dorsey High School|Dorsey High School]], and [[Cleveland High School (Los Angeles, California)|Cleveland High School]] in suburban [[Reseda, California]]. He averaged 27.2 points and 10.8 rebounds as a 2004 senior at Cleveland, earning 2004 CIF L.A. City Section, Los Angeles Times All-City and San Fernando Valley first team honors. Young shot 57.3% from the field and 46.8% from three-point range (52-of-111), had 48 steals and 41 blocks as Cleveland finished with a 25–4 record. He was tabbed the seventh-best player in the country by HoopScoop and listed by basketball columnist Frank Burlison as among the Top 50 recruits in 2004. Young once scored 56 points in one game and had 23 rebounds in another. He earned CIF L.A. City Section first team honors in 2003 and was included in a list of Top Seniors by ''[[Athlon Sports]]'' heading into 2004. ==College career== Young played for the [[University of Southern California]] from 2004 to 2007 and was [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10 First Team]] in the 2005–06 and 2006–07 seasons. In the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2007 NCAA Tournament]], he led the fifth-seeded Trojans to a berth in the Sweet Sixteen, where they lost to the one-seeded [[North Carolina Tar Heels]], 74–64.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=274000022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107005808/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=274000022 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 7, 2012 |title=UNC pulls off biggest rally of the season to dismiss USC |work=ESPN.com |date=March 23, 2007 |access-date=May 18, 2012}} Along the way, Young led USC to a 77–60 first-round win against Arkansas.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=274000019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110730033026/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=274000019 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 30, 2011 |title=Gibson keys decisive Trojan victory over Hogs |work=ESPN.com |date=March 16, 2007 |access-date=May 18, 2012}} In the second round, he led the team with 22 points over the [[Texas Longhorns]] in an 87–68 win which featured the National Player of the Year, [[Kevin Durant]], though Durant led both teams in scoring with 30.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=274000021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070322165013/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=274000021 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 22, 2007 |title=Young pours in 22 points for USC in blowout of Texas |work=ESPN.com |date=March 18, 2007 |access-date=May 18, 2012}} As expected, following his junior season,{{cite news|first=Andy|last=Katz|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2007/news/story?id=2839924 |title=Trojans' Young set to declare but may not get agent |work=ESPN.com |date=April 16, 2007 |access-date=May 18, 2012}} Young announced on April 15, 2007, to the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' that he would forgo his senior year and enter the [[2007 NBA draft]],{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2007/news/story?id=2841107 |title=USC's Young passes on senior year, turns pro |work=ESPN.com |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 17, 2007 |access-date=May 18, 2012}} where Young was selected with the 16th overall pick by the [[Washington Wizards]]. ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards (2007–2012)=== [[File:Nickyoungwizz.jpg|thumb|Young in 2008|left|337x337px]] Young was selected 16th overall by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2007 NBA draft]]. He started his first career NBA game on December 15, 2007, against the [[Sacramento Kings]]. On January 9, 2010, Young was fined $10,000 by the Wizards for participating in antics before a game on January 5, 2010, against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. [[Gilbert Arenas]] was being investigated for a prior incident involving guns in the Wizards' locker room, but made light of the accusations by pointing his finger at his teammates, as if he were shooting them. Young's teammates were photographed smiling and laughing with him.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4810297 |title=Wiz fine Blatche, McGee, Foye, Young|work=ESPN |date=January 9, 2010 |access-date=July 21, 2022}} Young scored a career-high 43 points on January 11, 2011, against the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2011/01/11/AR2011011107720.html |title=Wizards vs. Kings: Nick Young scores 43 and Washington survives meltdowns to win in overtime, 136-133 |work=The Washington Post |date=January 12, 2011 |access-date=May 18, 2012}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2012)=== On March 15, 2012, Young was traded to his hometown team the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in a three-way trade involving the [[Denver Nuggets]] and [[Washington Wizards]]. On April 16, 2012, Young helped the Clippers clinch their first playoff berth in six years with a 19-point performance against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. He was also a key part of the Clippers' comeback victory against the Memphis Grizzlies in game one of the first round of the 2012 playoffs, making three three-pointers in under a minute.{{Cite web |title=Clippers 92-77 Thunder (Apr 16, 2012) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/320416012 |access-date=2024-02-19 |website=ESPN |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2012-03-15 |title=Wizards' Nick Young of USC, Cleveland High traded to Clippers |url=https://www.dailynews.com/sports/20120315/wizards-nick-young-of-usc-cleveland-high-traded-to-clippers/ |access-date=2024-02-19 |website=Daily News |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Khan |first=Ehran |title=The Greatest Playoff Comeback in L.A. Clippers History |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1174596-the-greatest-playoff-comeback-in-la-clippers-history |access-date=2024-02-19 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2012–2013)=== On July 12, 2012, Young signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] to a one-year deal.[http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-free-agent-guard-nick-young Sixers Sign Free Agent Guard Nick Young] ===Los Angeles Lakers (2013–2017)=== On July 11, 2013, Young signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Nick Young|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/130711nickyoung|work=NBA.com|date=July 21, 2014|access-date=July 21, 2014}} During the [[2013–14 Los Angeles Lakers season|2013–14 season]], he converted a Lakers-record seven [[four-point play]]s while averaging a career-high 17.9 points per game.{{cite news|last=Markazi|first=Arash|title=Nick Young has torn thumb ligament|date=October 3, 2014|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/nba/story/_/id/11637061/nick-young-los-angeles-lakers-undergo-surgery-tearing-radial-collateral-ligament-right-thumb|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141004182712/http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/nba/story/_/id/11637061/nick-young-los-angeles-lakers-undergo-surgery-tearing-radial-collateral-ligament-right-thumb|archive-date=October 4, 2014|access-date=October 4, 2014|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}}{{cite web|title=LOS ANGELES LAKERS 2013-14 SEASON REVIEW|work=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/gamenotes/lakers.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141013101237/http://www.nba.com/gamenotes/lakers.pdf|archive-date=October 13, 2014|access-date=October 4, 2014|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} On July 21, 2014, Young re-signed with Lakers to a reported four-year, $21.5 million contract.{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Nick Young|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140721nickyoung_resign|work=NBA.com|date=July 21, 2014|access-date=July 27, 2014}}{{cite web|title=Nick Young Agrees To Re-Sign With Lakers On Four-Year, $21.5M Deal|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234235/Nick-Young-Agrees-To-Re-Sign-With-Lakers-On-Four-Year-$215M-Deal|work=RealGM.com|date=July 11, 2014|access-date=July 27, 2014}} During training camp, he suffered a complete tear of the [[radial collateral ligament of thumb|radial collateral ligament]] in his right thumb, and was expected to miss six to eight weeks. After missing the first 10 games of the season with the injury, Young made his season debut on November 18 against the Atlanta Hawks, recording 17 points and five rebounds in a 114–109 win.{{cite web|title=Bryant leads struggling Lakers past Hawks 114-109|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20141118/LALATL/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=November 18, 2014|access-date=November 19, 2014}} On December 12, he scored a season-high 29 points in a 112–110 victory over the San Antonio Spurs.{{cite web|title=Nick Young 2014-15 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/y/youngni01/gamelog/2015/|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 27, 2015}} On November 30, 2016, Young was ruled out for two to four weeks due to a strained right calf muscle.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2016/11/30/lakers-nick-young-out-2-4-weeks-strained-calf|title=Lakers' Nick Young to miss 2-4 weeks with calf injury|work=NBA.com|date=November 30, 2016|access-date=November 30, 2016}} On December 17, he made eight three-pointers and scored a season-high 32 points in a 119–108 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899844|title=LeBron scores 16 in fourth as Cavs outlast Lakers 119-108|work=ESPN.com|date=December 17, 2016|access-date=December 18, 2016}} Between late December and early January, Young's burst from long range gave him 36 three-pointers in eight games—the most in an eight-game stretch in Lakers franchise history.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899387|title=Kyle Lowry scores 41 as Raptors hold off Lakers, 123-114|work=ESPN.com|date=January 1, 2017|access-date=January 2, 2017}} On April 2, 2017, after being held out of 11 of the previous 12 games despite being healthy, Young was shut down by the Lakers for the last five regular-season games.{{cite web|last=Medina|first=Mark|title=Lakers' D'Angelo Russell takes 'huge step forward' during game against Grizzlies|url=https://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170402/lakers-dangelo-russell-takes-huge-step-forward-during-game-against-grizzlies|access-date=April 3, 2017|work=DailyNews.com|date=April 2, 2017}} On June 21, 2017, the Lakers announced that Young elected not to exercise his option to extend his contract for the 2017–18 season, thus becoming an unrestricted free agent.{{cite web|title=Nick Young Becomes Free Agent|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/170621-nick-young-declines-option|website=NBA.com|access-date=June 22, 2017|date=June 21, 2017}} ===Golden State Warriors (2017–2018)=== On July 7, 2017, Young signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/nick-young-signed-20170707|title=Warriors Sign Free Agent Guard Nick Young|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2017|access-date=July 7, 2017}} During his Warriors debut in their season opener on October 17, Young came off the bench to hit six three-pointers and score 23 points in a narrow 122–121 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974438|title=Rockets rally to spoil defending champion Warriors return|work=ESPN.com|date=October 17, 2017|access-date=October 17, 2017}} He helped the Warriors reach the [[2018 NBA Finals]], where they defeated the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in a four-game sweep, with Young winning his first NBA championship. ===Denver Nuggets (2018)=== On December 10, 2018, Young signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets Sign Nick Young, Waive Brandon Goodwin|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-nick-young-waive-goodwin-121018-2|website=NBA.com|date=December 10, 2018|access-date=December 10, 2018}} He was waived on December 30 after appearing in only four games.{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets waive guard Nick Young|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2018/12/30/denver-nuggets-waive-nick-young|website=NBA.com|date=December 30, 2018|access-date=December 31, 2018}} === Macau Black Bears (2023) === On September 26, 2023, Young signed with the [[Macau Black Bears]] of The Asian Tournament (TAT),{{cite news|first=Emiliano|last=Carchia|title=Macau Black Bears sign Nick Young and Liu Chuanxing|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/macau-black-bears-sign-nick-young-and-liu-chuanxing/|newspaper=Sportando|date=October 2, 2023|access-date=October 2, 2023}}{{cite news |author=曾曉瀅 {{Short description|Australian singer-songwriter (born 1990)|bot=PearBOT 5}} {{Use dmy dates|date=September 2020}} {{Use Australian English|date=March 2012}} {{Infobox musical artist | name = Matt Corby | background = solo_singer | image = Matt Corby (193022).jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Corby performing in [[Oslo]] in 2016 | birth_name = Matthew John Corby | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1990|11|7|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Oyster Bay, New South Wales]], Australia | genre = {{hlist|[[Indie rock]]|[[folk music|folk]]|[[Acoustic music|acoustic]]|[[blue-eyed soul]]|[[alternative rock|alternative]]}} | occupation = {{hlist|Musician|singer-songwriter}} | instrument = {{hlist|Vocals|guitar|piano|[[banjo]]|harmonica|[[glockenspiel]]|[[Electronic keyboard|keyboard]]|flute|[[hang (instrument)|hang]]|bass guitar|drums}} | years_active = 2007–present | label = {{hlist|Scorpio|[[Communion Music|Communion]]|Atlantic|Elektra|[[Universal Music Australia]]|Mercury Records Australia | Rainbow Valley Records }} | website = {{URL|mattcorby.com}} }} '''Matthew John Corby''' (born 7 November 1990){{cite web|url=https://www.bodeganottingham.com/gigs/matt-corby/#:~:text=Matthew%20John%20Corby%20was%20born,runner%2Dup%20to%20Natalie%20Gauci|title=Matt Corby|website=Bodeganottingham.com|access-date=16 April 2026}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.nika.si/Izvajalci/MATT_CORBY/|title=MATT CORBY|website=Nika.si|access-date=16 April 2026}} is an Australian singer-songwriter. He achieved his commercial breakthrough with his fourth EP, ''[[Into the Flame]]'' (2011), which peaked at No. 3 on the [[ARIA Charts|ARIA Singles Chart]], and by April 2012, was certified 6× Platinum by [[Australian Recording Industry Association|ARIA]]. His 2011 single "[[Brother (Matt Corby song)|Brother]]" and his 2013 single "[[Resolution (Matt Corby song)|Resolution]]" both won [[ARIA Music Award]]s for [[ARIA Award for Song of the Year|Song of the Year]]. Corby has released four studio albums, ''[[Telluric (album)|Telluric]]'' (2016), ''[[Rainbow Valley (album)|Rainbow Valley]]'' (2018), ''[[Everything's Fine (Matt Corby album)|Everything's Fine]]'' (2023) and ''[[Tragic Magic (Matt Corby album)|Tragic Magic]]'' (2026). ==Early life== Matthew Corby was born in Sydney, Australia,{{Cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/gb/artist/matt-corby/268919290|title=Matt Corby|via=[[Apple Music]]|access-date=16 April 2026}} and raised in [[Oyster Bay, New South Wales]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.news.com.au/entertainment/everyone-loves-matt/story-e6frfo60-1111114860662|title=Everyone loves Matt|work=[[News.com.au]]| date=November 13, 2007|access-date=26 July 2018|archive-date=30 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230051925/http://www.news.com.au/entertainment/everyone-loves-matt/story-e6frfo60-1111114860662|url-status=dead| quote= the 17-year-old Sutherland Shire singer...}} Corby's earliest musical memory is being driven past a guitar shop as a five-year-old and being captivated by the rows of shiny instruments in the window. His father John bought his son a three-quarter acoustic guitar for $80, on which Corby started having one lesson a week. The first song he learned to play was "[[Greensleeves]]".{{cite web|access-date=7 March 2023|author=Rod Yates|date=April 2016|title=Matt Corby: The Reluctant Star|url=https://au.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/matt-corby-feature-1141/|website=[[Rolling Stone Australia]]}}{{Cite web|title=Inside Matt Corby's Reclusive Rainforest Life|url=https://lnwy.co/read/inside-matt-corbys-reclusive-rainforest-life/|access-date=2021-06-23|website=LNWY|language=en-US|archive-date=24 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624205350/https://lnwy.co/read/inside-matt-corbys-reclusive-rainforest-life/|url-status=dead}} Corby attended [[Inaburra School]] in [[Bangor, New South Wales]]{{cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/articles/2007/11/16/1194766964056.html?page=fullpage#contentSwap1|title=Taking sides for the idol cause|first=Andrew|last=Hornery|date=17 November 2007|work=Sydney Morning Herald}} where he grew up steeped in gospel; his passion for music fed first by renditions of "[[His Eye is on the Sparrow]]" and later by a love for [[Crosby, Stills, Nash and Young]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.rockhal.lu/fr/the-rockhal/past-shows/show/detail/matt-corby-1/|title=Rockhal: MATT CORBY|website=www.rockhal.lu|language=fr-FR|access-date=26 July 2018|archive-date=26 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180726104214/https://www.rockhal.lu/fr/the-rockhal/past-shows/show/detail/matt-corby-1/|url-status=dead}} Corby attended [[Shirelive]] church with his family.{{Cite news|date=2007-11-12|title=God, girls, bookies: everyone loves Matt Corby|url=https://www.news.com.au/entertainment/everyone-loves-matt/news-story/be291d72d40221da69a3166574a18444|access-date=2021-06-23|newspaper=News.com.au|language=en|last1=Byrne's|first1=By Holly}} Corby's school principal encouraged him to sing at a school assembly where he performed a song from ''[[Sister Act 2: Back in the Habit|Sister Act 2]]''.{{Cite web|last=Sehmar|first=Paras|date=2019-02-15|title=Matt Corby // Interview {{!}} LONDON IN STEREO|url=https://www.londoninstereo.com/matt-corby-interview/|access-date=2021-06-23|language=en-US}} By the time he was 10, Corby had been trained classically by an opera singer and was making tentative steps into musical theatre, playing a minor role in a production of ''Cain and Abel'' and [[Sutherland Shire|Sutherland Shire Light Opera Company]]'s take on ''[[The Secret Garden]]''. At age 13, Corby joined a church band called Iron and Clay,{{Cite news|url=https://www.stawelltimes.com.au/story/221385/iron-and-clay-to-perform-in-stawell/|title=Iron and Clay to perform in Stawell|date=1 March 2012|work=The Stawell Times-News|access-date=26 July 2018|language=en}} Corby left the group just before his 16th birthday, and got a job making sandwiches at [[Subway (restaurant)|Subway]] before going back to school in Year 11, which coincided with his ''Australian Idol'' appearance. ==Career== ===2007: ''Australian Idol''=== {{main|Australian Idol (season 5)}} [[File:Photo by band member Jack Standen .jpg|alt=|thumb]] At age 16, Corby auditioned for the [[Australian Idol (season 5)|fifth season]] of ''[[Australian Idol]]'', where he finished as runner-up. Years later, he described participating in the competition as being a "big fucking mistake",{{cite news|url=http://www.news.com.au/entertainment/music/why-australian-idol-runnerup-matt-corby-is-glad-his-days-on-reality-tv-are-behind-him/news-story/7de94bc9281bf4555830df8063a5cc09|title=Why Australian Idol runner-up Matt Corby is glad his days on reality TV are behind him |newspaper=News.com.au |date= 7 March 2016|access-date=21 May 2017|last1=McCabe |first1=Kathy }} describing how the struggle to forge his own identity post-''Idol'' was bigger than most could have seen from the outside. "I took all the negatives out of that (''Idol'') and thought 'Bugger, I've ruined everything'". One aspect of ''Australian Idol'' that the media speculated about was the number of Christian musicians among the finalists. The media suggested that Christians were "stacking" the voting to keep "their" artists on the show. Matt Corby | align="center"| Runner-Up |} After the Idol finale, Corby passed on a record deal offered by [[Sony Music Australia]]. The week after he turned 18, Corby landed in London, staying in a friend's attic. ===2009–2010: ''Song for...'', ''My False'' and ''Transition to Colour'' EPs=== {{main|Transition to Colour}} On 5 June 2009, Corby independently released his debut extended play, ''Song for...'', with Scorpio Music. Whilst in London, Corby met with indie label [[Communion Music]] and found himself encouraged to learn the craft of songwriting, to understand the marriage between the force of his voice and the words it carries.{{Cite news|url=https://thewest.com.au/news/wa/matt-corbys-down-to-earth-debut-ng-ya-100996|title=Matt Corby finally releases his debut album|date=1 March 2016|work=The West Australian|access-date=26 July 2018|language=en-GB}} In 2010, Corby released two EPs with Communion, ''My False'' and ''[[Transition to Colour]]'', but was forced home when he ran out of money, having accrued a debt of around $80,000. Corby's track "Made of Stone" was featured on an episode of ''[[Underbelly: Razor]]'' in 2011 and on ABC's ''[[Brothers & Sisters (2006 TV series)|Brothers and Sisters]]''. "Lighthome" was in an episode of ''[[Home and Away]]'' in 2011, and "Song for..." in 2012 on the same TV series. Corby recorded a cover version of [[INXS]]'s "[[By My Side (INXS song)|By My Side]]" for the band's album, ''[[Original Sin (INXS album)|Original Sin]]'', as a bonus track for the iTunes edition. He was featured on a track on [[Julia Stone]]'s debut solo album, ''[[Julia Stone#The Memory Machine (2010)|The Memory Machine]]'', and on UK singer-songwriter [[Passenger (singer)|Passenger]]'s track "Golden Thread", from the 2010 album ''Flight of the Crow''. The EP also featured in ''[[The Blacklist (TV series)|The Blacklist]]'' starring [[James Spader]]. ===2011–2012: ''Into the Flame'' EP and "Brother"=== {{main|Into the Flame}} After a few months of writing, Corby spent September 2011 recording his fourth EP, ''[[Into the Flame]]'', with producer Tim Carr. The EP showcased a new direction for Corby, including [[Soul music|soul]]-influenced, growling vocals along with a [[Blues music|bluesy]] melody, in conjunction with Corby's signature folk style. The title song has been described as "lyrically raw and endearingly honest". The EP also features a duet with keyboardist Bree Tranter, previously a part of Australian band, [[The Middle East (band)|The Middle East]]. The EP provided Corby's first entry on the [[ARIA Charts]], where it reached No. 46 on the ARIA Top 50 Singles Chart on 4 December 2011. It subsequently peaked at No. 3.{{cite web | url = http://australian-charts.com/showitem.asp?interpret=Matt+Corby&titel=Into+The+Flame+%5BEP%5D&cat=s | title = Matt Corby – ''Into the Flame'' (EP) | publisher = Australian Charts Portal. Hung Medien | access-date = 9 December 2011 }} Upon its release, Corby posted a message on his website and Facebook page: {{blockquote|After 12 months of lots of ups and downs, I'm so excited to share this EP with you. I honestly felt like giving up music back in April but all of you inspired me again. It's been an incredible few months re-connecting with all of you in gardens around Australia. Thank you from the bottom of my heart for all your support. It's been said by others before... but you guys really are the best fans ever. Let's stay close on this journey.}} By December 2012, ''Into the Flame'' achieved 6× platinum certification by ARIA. Corby supported the release of his EP and its single "[[Brother (Matt Corby song)|Brother]]" with a national into the Flame Tour. It included a mini Secret Garden Summer Tour around New South Wales. In January 2012, Corby was named the 'Next Big Thing' and won 'Song of the Year' for "Brother" at FBi Radio's annual SMAC Awards in [[Darlinghurst, New South Wales]]. He premiered his rendition of [[The Black Keys]]' song, "[[Lonely Boy (The Black Keys song)|Lonely Boy]]", for radio station [[Triple J]]'s segment, ''[[Like a Version]]'', with hosts [[Tom Ballard (comedian)|Tom]] and [[Alex Dyson|Alex]], along with an acoustic rendition of his own song, "Brother". Both have since received significant attention online. Corby secured a support slot with [[Feist (singer)|Feist]] in Adelaide on her 2012 Australian tour. Early in 2012, he toured throughout the US and UK. Corby's song "Brother" was voted into the No. 3 position for the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2011]], and his cover of "Lonely Boy" was voted at No. 69 in the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2012]]. Corby released a Digital iTunes Session EP on 7 December 2012, playing five of his songs from his previous EP's acoustically on guitar and one on piano, as well as a rendition of "Amazing Grace". Corby spent the first half of 2013 in Los Angeles, working on his upcoming record, due for release later that year. Corby was nominated for three 2012 ARIA Music Awards, including two nominations in industry voted categories, [[ARIA Award for Breakthrough Artist - Release|Breakthrough Artist]] and [[ARIA Award for Best Male Artist|Best Male Artist]].{{cite web | url = http://www.abc.net.au/triplej/musicnews/s3337827.htm | title = Nominations > Breakthrough Artist – 2012 | publisher = Triple J | Triple J | year = 2012 | access-date = 10 October 2012 }} He won the publicly voted Song of the Year category.[https://web.archive.org/web/20121203045649/http://www.ariaawards.com.au/news/46/arias-2012 2012 Winners announced].Australian Recording Industry Association. 29 November 2012. Archived from [http://www.ariaawards.com.au/news/46/arias-2012 the original] on 29 November 2012 The newly recorded version of 'Made of Stone' can be heard on the [[NCIS (TV series)|NCIS]] television promo in the USA.[http://entertainment.gather.com/viewArticle.action?articleId=281474981600459 Gather Entertainment: NCIS Promo] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140727231856/http://entertainment.gather.com/viewArticle.action?articleId=281474981600459 |date=27 July 2014 }} Gather Entertainment. Retrieved 30 September 2012. Matt was featured on a [[Hunters & Collectors]] tribute album collaborating with Australian artist [[Missy Higgins]], recording a version of "This Morning". ===2013–2014: ''Resolution''=== {{main|Resolution (EP)}} On 21 May 2013, Corby released "[[Resolution (Matt Corby song)|Resolution]]". It became his first charting single, peaked at number 3 on the [[ARIA Charts]]. The song also charted in New Zealand and the United Kingdom, becoming his first charting material in those countries. On 12 July 2013, the ''[[Resolution (EP)|Resolution EP]]'' was released, containing the single and three new original songs. One of which, "Lay You Down", entered the ARIA Charts at number 75 despite receiving no independent promotion. "Resolution" was voted in eighth place in [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2013]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/triplej/hottest100/13/countdown/|title=Hottest 100 – 2013 {{!}} triple j|date=1 September 2013|website=www.abc.net.au|access-date=26 September 2016}} In December 2013, "Resolution" won the [[ARIA Award for Song of the Year]]. On 13 December, Corby released the ''[[Live On the Resolution Tour]]'' EP. Its five original songs were recorded live at the Australian and New Zealand shows, including a cover of [[Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young]]'s "[[Almost Cut My Hair]]". Corby got involved with a Brisbane-based arts collective called "Museum Collective", described on their Facebook page{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/museumcollective|title=Security Check Required|via=[[Facebook]]}} as an "Audio Visual Sensory Experience". The band also features Rohin Jones (who is Museum Collective's musical director), Bree Tranter & Michael Haydon, formerly of [[The Middle East (band)|The Middle East]], as well as Lyndon de la Cruz, Kahl Wallis (of [[The Medics]]), Bud Rokesky and Tom Wearne. Museum Collective ran free performances at Brisbane's Old Museum building in September & December and also at Woodford Folk Festival on 28 December 2013.{{Cite web|url=https://www.museumcollective.com.au/|title=Index of /|website=Museumcollective.com.au|access-date=7 July 2023}} In January 2014, Corby released the song "What the Devil Has Made", arranged specifically for the ''[[Spirit of Akasha]]'' soundtrack. The surf documentary was inspired by the 1971 film, ''[[Morning of the Earth]]''. He recorded all parts of the track – including harmonies, flute and guitar – on his own in his home studio. The soundtrack also features Corby's version of Tamam Shud's "First Things First" (originally used in the 1971 film). Also in February 2014, Corby's song "Breathe", from his 2010 EP ''Transition to Colour'', was featured in the closing scenes of the 21st episode of the fourth season of the popular US teen drama / mystery thriller TV series ''[[Pretty Little Liars]]'', titled "[[Pretty Little Liars (season 4)|She's Come Undone]]".{{Cite web|url=https://www.tunefind.com/show/pretty-little-liars/season-4/16448|title=Tunefind|website=Tunefind.com|access-date=7 July 2023}} ===2015–2017: "Monday" and ''Telluric''=== {{main|Telluric (album)}} [[File:Matt Corby (193603).jpg|thumb|Matt Corby performs at Piknik i Parken in Oslo in June 2016]] On 1 October 2015, Corby released his first song in two years, "[[Monday (Matt Corby song)|Monday]]" from his debut album, ''[[Telluric (album)|Telluric]]''. The song was described as containing "lush, transcendent harmonies, wailing falsetto, folky boom-claps and heartbreaking lyrics." The song reportedly took 10 minutes to record, and was laid down in a cottage in the NSW coastal town of [[Berry, New South Wales|Berry]] where he wrote and recorded most of the album. Corby said to Matt and Alex of [[Triple J]]: "It's stomping on the ground and clapping. It feels good to have that as a composition in a weird way, it's just your voice and everyone who would maybe want to do a cover of that if they so wish, it'll always sound different because they'll have to harmonise with their own [voice]."{{Cite web|url=http://www.abc.net.au/triplej/musicnews/s4322989.htm|title=Matt Corby premieres new single 'Monday', announces national tour {{!}} Music News {{!}} triple j|website=abc.net.au|access-date=26 September 2016}} "Monday" was voted number 53 in the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2015]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/triplej/hottest100/15/countdown/|title=1–100 List {{!}} Hottest 100 2015 {{!}} triple j|date=1 January 2014|website=www.abc.net.au|access-date=26 September 2016}} ''Telluric'' was released on 11 March 2016.{{cite web|url=http://www.getmusic.com.au/store/matt-corby-telluric-mp3-digital-album-5984451|title=Telluric MP3|work=Get Music|access-date=10 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151211025534/http://www.getmusic.com.au/store/matt-corby-telluric-mp3-digital-album-5984451|archive-date=11 December 2015|url-status=dead}} American artist, [[Gary Burden]], designed the album cover. It debuted at number one in Australia.{{Cite web|url=http://www.ariacharts.com.au/news/2016/matt-corby-scores-first-1-with-telluric|title=Matt Corby Scores First #1 With Telluric|publisher=ARIA Charts}} Corby was featured on the track "Serious" from Norwegian DJ [[Kygo]]'s debut album ''[[Cloud Nine (Kygo album)|Cloud Nine]]'', released on 13 May 2016. === 2018–2021: ''Rainbow Valley'' === {{main|Rainbow Valley (album)}} Corby released his first song in two years, "No Ordinary Life", on 3 August 2018. On 7 September 2018, Corby announced his second studio album ''[[Rainbow Valley]]'' would be released on 2 November 2018. Upon release, the album was the highest local debut of the week in Australia, debuting at number 4 on the ARIA charts.{{Cite web|url=https://themusic.com.au/article/FBYMBgkICwo/matt-corby-makes-highest-local-debut-as-king-gizzard-flood-the-aria-album-charts|title=/|website=The Music|language=en|access-date=22 February 2019}} He also subsequently released the second, third and fourth singles from the album, titled "[[All Fired Up (Matt Corby song)|All Fired Up]]", "All That I See" and "[[Miracle Love]]". [[File:Matt Corby Williams Green Glastonbury Festival 2019 -012.jpg|thumb|Matt Corby performing at Williams Green Glastonbury Festival 2019]] In February 2019, Matt released a mini-documentary, ''Behind Rainbow Valley'', documenting the recording and creative process of the ''Rainbow Valley'' album. Speaking of the influence of his newborn son Hugh on the creation of the album, Corby stated: "I wanted to create something that was almost instructional for my little boy... A reference for him of the way I see reality and the simple truths that I've come across. The lyrics are simple truths. I'm not trying to be too clever or poetic. If anything it was, 'This is the way I see the world and this is the way I feel about it'."{{Cite web|url=https://themusicnetwork.com/matt-corby-drops-doco-behind-making-of-rainbow-valley/|title=Matt Corby drops doco behind making of Rainbow Valley|date=1 February 2019|website=The Music Network|access-date=22 February 2019}} Corby embarked on the 2019 Rainbow Valley Tour in Europe, the UK, Australia and New Zealand but many dates were cancelled due to the pandemic towards the end of the tour.{{Cite web|title=Matt Corby - Postponed|url=http://www.commodoreballroom.com/view-all/2019/9/29/mattcorby|access-date=23 June 2021|website=The Commodore Ballroom|language=en-US|archive-date=24 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624210847/http://www.commodoreballroom.com/view-all/2019/9/29/mattcorby|url-status=dead}}{{Cite web|last=Newstead|first=Al|date=29 October 2018|title=Matt Corby announces Australian tour for 'Rainbow Valley'|url=https://www.abc.net.au/triplej/news/musicnews/matt-corby-announces-australian-tour-2019-rainbow-valley-album/10433816|access-date=2021-06-23|website=triple j|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=Corby|first=Matt|title=Matt Corby Rainbow Valley Tour|url=https://twitter.com/mattcorby/status/1123304244755361792|access-date=23 June 2021|website=Twitter|language=en}} Corby was announced as the replacement for [[Ziggy Marley]] after he dropped out at [[WOMADelaide|WOMAD]] 2020, in Adelaide.{{Cite web|date=6 March 2020|title=Matt Corby replaces Ziggy Marley on WOMADelaide lineup|url=https://www.nme.com/en_au/news/music/matt-corby-replaces-ziggy-marley-on-womadelaide-lineup-2621351|access-date=23 June 2021|website=NME|language=en-AU}} In 2020 Corby released the singles "If I Never Say a Word" and "Vitamin".{{cn|date=May 2025}} === 2022–present: ''Everything's Fine'' === {{main|Everything's Fine (Matt Corby album)}} In November 2022, Corby released his first single in two years, "[[Problems (Matt Corby song)|Problems]]".{{cite web |url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/listen-matt-corby-smooth-single-004135842.html|title=Listen to Matt Corby's Smooth New Single 'Problems' |publisher=[[Yahoo]]|date=3 November 2022 |access-date=4 November 2022 }} In January 2023, Corby announced the release date of his third studio album, ''[[Everything's Fine (Matt Corby album)|Everything's Fine]]'', alongside the release of its second single, "[[Reelin']]". ''Everything's Fine'' was released on 24 March 2023.{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/en_au/news/music/matt-corby-details-new-album-everythings-fine-shares-single-reelin-3379023|title=Matt Corby details new album ''Everything's Fine'', shares single 'Reelin''|website=[[NME]]|date=13 January 2023|access-date=14 January 2023}} In February 2025, Corby produced "Call Me When You Get In", a song by [[Harrison Storm]].{{cite web|url=https://happymag.tv/new-music-friday-28-02-2025/|title=New Music Friday featuring The Pretty Littles, aleksiah, Teether and Kuya Neil|website=Happy Mag TV|date=28 February 2025|access-date=2 March 2025}} In September 2025, Corby released the single "Long and Short" ahead of his supporting [[Teddy Swims]] on his Australian ''[[I've Tried Everything but Therapy]]'' tour in October 2025.{{cite web|url=https://au.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/matt-corby-new-single-long-and-short-83367/|title=Matt Corby Releases Highly Anticipated New Single "Long and Short"|website=[[Rolling Stone Australia]]|date=12 September 2025|access-date=14 September 2025|author=ALEC JONES}} Corby's fourth studio album ''[[Tragic Magic (Matt Corby album)|Tragic Magic]]'' was released on 17 April 2026.{{cite web|url=https://au.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/matt-corby-tragic-magic-announcement-85770/|title=Matt Corby Channels Motown and Magic on New Album, Announced Today|website=[[Rolling Stone Australia]]|date=17 October 2025|access-date=19 October 2025}} ==Personal life== [[File:Matt Corby crop.jpg|thumb|Corby performing at [[Easterfest]] 2008]] Corby and his sister Grace grew up in the Christian faith after their parents became Christian when Corby was two years old. Corby would sing in church and stated in 2008, "When I was 13, I started touring with a ministry team and we went around schools and churches, promoting Jesus and tackling depression issues and stuff like that. I did that for a couple of years. So I've sort of been in church my whole life and it's been fun". Going into ''Australian Idol'', Corby wondered how his faith would fit in with the show, but stated that it made him self-reliant and brought him closer to God through his own personal drive into Bible study. Corby headlined [[Easterfest]], a Christian music festival in 2008 and a [[Hillsong Church|Hillsong]] United convention.{{Cite web|date=5 August 2011|title=Post-Worship Songs|url=https://www.abc.net.au/radionational/programs/archived/rhythmdivine/post-worship-songs/4718096|access-date=2021-06-23|website=Radio National|language=en-AU}}{{Citation|title=Hillsong Conference 2008- Matt Corby|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2omnSsDkoc0| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624212800/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2omnSsDkoc0| archive-date=2021-06-24 | url-status=dead|language=en|access-date=23 June 2021}} Although growing up as a strong Christian, Corby is no longer religious, but does understand the draw of a church for young families in particular to have a community connection and collective moral of kindness. Corby once stated: "I'm a stoner and I don't really have much sympathy for religion any more, I basically believe that human beings are pure entities when they're born, and they have the ability to do whatever they want to change the Earth in a positive way. And it's just... they get lied to, and in the process of becoming an adult that ends up fucking up the world."{{Cite web|url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/amen-brother-the-testament-of-matt-corby|title=Amen, Brother: The Testament of Matt Corby|date=16 March 2016 }} By the time he was 20 he was reading books on philosophy and neuroscience, the latter because he wanted to know how the brain functions, partly because of his experiences with depression and anxiety. "People have said I have depression before, especially when I was younger. People were like, you should really go see someone. But I just thought, no, I'm pretty sure the human brain is capable of so much more than what I'm being told I'm capable of. When people say you need help it's like, do I? With what? And if you could just tell me what I need help with, couldn't I just go and work on it myself?" His search for self led him to spiritual authors such as [[Eckhart Tolle]], and to experimenting with [[Psilocybin mushroom|magic mushrooms]]: "You take mushrooms and then you go, I have no problems," he explains. "I am an ant walking around this planet in a speck in the middle of nowhere. And that's the truth, it's all we are."[http://rollingstoneaus.com/music/post/matt-corby-feature/3704-page-1 Matt Corby feature] rollingstoneaus.com {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160504162754/http://rollingstoneaus.com/music/post/matt-corby-feature/3704-page-1 |date=4 May 2016 }} Corby's musical influences include artists such as [[Jeff Buckley]], [[Lauryn Hill]], [[Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young]], [[Sufjan Stevens]], [[Patrick Watson (musician)|Patrick Watson]], [[Scott Mathews]], [[Nick Drake]], [[Nina Simone]], [[Otis Redding]], [[Bon Iver]], [[Bob Dylan]], [[Buddy Guy]], [[Charles Bradley (singer)|Charles Bradley]] and [[Sam Cooke]].{{Cite web|title=Matt Corby|url=https://sungenre.com/artist/matt-corby/|access-date=23 June 2021|website=Sungenre}} Corby is good friends with Australian musician [[Jarryd James]], whom Corby credits with having helped with his musical development.{{Cite web|last=Newstead|first=Al|date=2019-11-29|title=Jarryd James and Matt Corby have "20 hard drives" of songs recorded together|url=https://www.abc.net.au/triplej/news/musicnews/jarryd-james-matt-corby-recorded-songs-together-like-a-version/11749384|access-date=23 June 2021|website=.abc.net.au}} In early 2018, Corby became a father with his first child Hugh.{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/triplej/news/musicnews/first-spin:-matt-corbys-new-song-is-inspired-by-willy-wonka-an/10066752|title = First Spin: Matt Corby's new song is inspired by Willy Wonka and fatherhood|website = [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]]|date = 3 August 2018}} Speaking to ''Beat Magazine'' regarding the way fatherhood has changed his perspective, he stated: "Most of my life, music has been the number one focus. And now it sort of doesn't fit in that category anymore – it's really important, but, it's not as important as my child...When I come back to music, I'm then a lot happier and it's not like I'm constantly exposing myself to only music, and then getting really annoyed about it, or getting hard on myself."{{Cite web|url=http://www.beat.com.au/music/matt-corby-moving-country-starting-family-his-simplified-new-album|title=Matt Corby on moving to the country, starting a family and his simplified new album|website=Beat Magazine|language=en|access-date=22 February 2019}} Corby plays guitar, piano, drums, flute amongst other instruments.{{Cite web|last=Sehmar|first=Paras|date=2019-02-15|title=Matt Corby // Interview {{!}} BERLIN IN STEREO|url=https://berlininstereo.com/matt-corby-interview/|access-date=23 June 2021|language=en-US}} Corby currently resides with his Kelpie Django, partner and two '''Matt Williams''' (born December 14, 1987) is an American former [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Placekicker|kicker]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech Red Raiders]]. He was offered the position to replace two struggling kickers on the roster in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sweetwaterreporter.com/content/view/116496/122/ |title=Sweetwater Reporter – Student who won contest might kick for Texas Tech |publisher=Sweetwaterreporter.com |date=October 25, 2008 |accessdate=2008-12-02}} {{Dead link|date=November 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/mike-leach-the-mad-scientist-of-football/|title=Mike Leach: The Mad Scientist of Football|website=[[60 Minutes]]|first=Scott|last=Pelley|date=December 31, 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151209211031/http://www.cbsnews.com/news/mike-leach-the-mad-scientist-of-football|archive-date=December 9, 2015}}</ref>

==Early life==
Williams attended [[Weatherford High School (Texas)|Weatherford High School]] in [[Weatherford, Texas]], where he played soccer and football. In football, he played both wide receiver and kicker. His signature moment as a kicker occurred when he kicked a 49-yard field goal through the uprights to defeat rival [[Mineral Wells Independent School District|Mineral Wells High School]] in overtime. He graduated from Weatherford in 2006.<ref name=Kate-DMN-11-21>{{cite news|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/dn/latestnews/stories/112208dnspotechkicker.3e801d3.html|title=Texas Tech kicker taking an unlikely road to stardom|publisher=Dallas Morning News|accessdate=2008-11-22|date=2008-11-22|author=Hairopoulos, Kate|archive-date=2008-12-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081208004015/http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/dn/latestnews/stories/112208dnspotechkicker.3e801d3.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==

===Tarleton State===
Williams [[Walk-on (sport term)|walked on]] to the [[Tarleton State Texans football]] team, though was only on the team for a month and never played a game.<ref name=Kate-DMN-11-21/>

===Texas Tech===
After two years at Tarleton State, Williams transferred to [[Texas Tech University|Texas Tech]]. During halftime of Tech's September 20, 2008, football game against the [[University of Massachusetts]], Williams entered a promotional contest in which he made a 30-yard field goal. He caught the attention of head coach [[Mike Leach (American football coach)|Mike Leach]], who liked the fundamentals he used on the kick. Leach wanted him on the team, and although it was initially thought he would not be immediately eligible, the [[NCAA]] granted a one-time exception based on the specific circumstances.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sports.mobile.msn.com/en-us/articles.aspx?aid=8706174&acid=2&afid=&avid=86128 |title=No headline – FOX Sports – Article |publisher=Sports.mobile.msn.com |accessdate=2008-12-02 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714123605/http://sports.mobile.msn.com/en-us/articles.aspx?aid=8706174&acid=2&afid=&avid=86128 |archivedate=2011-07-14 }}</ref> He was allowed to play immediately as he had not been recruited by Tarleton State and also because he was never a scholarship player. However, the season he played on Tarleton State's squad counted toward his eligibility, making him a sophomore during his first year at Tech. He also had to reject the free rent he won in the contest in order to remain eligible.<ref name=Kate-DMN-11-21/>

Williams made his debut in a 63–21 win over [[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas]] where he converted on all nine extra point attempts.<ref>{{cite news|last=Hairopoulos|first=Kate|author2=Carlton, Chuck|title=Walk-on Texas Tech kicker's role might expand|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=2008-10-29|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/colleges/texastech/stories/103008dnspotechtexasnotes.36a795a.html?npc|accessdate=2008-11-11}}{{Dead link|date=August 2023}}</ref> Following the game, Williams was recognized as the [[AT&T ESPN All-America Player|AT&T ESPN All-America Player of the Week]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Williams|first=Don|author2=Walker, Jeff|title=Red Raiders Football Notebook 10-31-2008|date=2008-10-31|url=http://www.redraiders.com/?p=3016|accessdate=2008-10-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160125213905/http://www.redraiders.com/?p=3016|archive-date=2016-01-25}}</ref>

The following week, in Texas Tech's 39–33 victory over [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas]], Williams was also asked to kick field goals, making two and having one blocked.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/colleges/texastech/stories/110508dnspoleach.17fa8414e.html?npc|title=Same drill on choosing the Texas Tech kicker, Leach says | Texas Tech Red Raiders News | Sports News | News for Dallas, Texas | Dallas Morning News|publisher=Dallasnews.com|date=November 5, 2008|access-date=2008-12-02}}{{Dead link|date=August 2023}}</ref>

In 2009, Williams made a career long 43-yard Field Goal against [[Baylor University]] in a 20–13 victory. {{cn|date=February 2023}}

Williams finished his career 149–150 on extra points and 22–28 (78.6%) on field goals. As of November 2025, he is 5th on the Red Raiders kickers scoring list with 215 career points.<ref>{{cite web |title=Texas Tech Red Raiders Kicking Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/texas-tech/kicking.html |website=[[Sports Reference]] |date=November 19, 2025 |access-date=November 19, 2025}}</ref>  He graduated in 2010.{{cn|date=February 2023}}

==Post-football career==

Matthew Williams currently works at Weatherford High school, Weatherford, TX, as a coach for boys football and girls soccer. He also teaches U.S. History and World History. <ref>{{Cite web |title=About me |url=https://whs-hs.weatherfordisd.com/apps/pages/index.jsp?uREC_ID=2513164&type=u&pREC_ID=2485514 |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=whs-hs.weatherfordisd.com |language=en}}</ref>

[[Lauren Young]] (cousin) | spouse = {{marriage|[[Pancho Magno]]|December 11, 2017|2023|end=div.}} | children = 1 }} '''Isabelle''' "'''Max'''" '''Abiera Collins''' (born August 28, 1992) is a Filipino actress and model. She is currently an exclusive artist of [[GMA Network]], where she has appeared in several of the network's television shows. ==Early life== Isabelle Abiera Collins was born on August 28, 1992 in [[Vallejo, California]], United States. Her mother is a Filipino from [[Kalibo, Aklan]] whilst her father is an American of [[Irish people|Irish]]-[[Italian people|Italian]] descent. Her parents met in [[Los Angeles]] while her mother was working at [[Bloomingdale's]]. Her parents separated when she was four years old. Her mother remarried when she was 9 years old. She has a younger half-brother. Collins, along with her family, moved from Vallejo to Kalibo when she was 10 years old. For four years, she lived in [[Boracay]] and attended [[Brent International School|Brent School Boracay]]. ==Career== ===2006–2010: Early years in ABS–CBN=== Collins started doing commercials when she was 10. She has also appeared in magazines like Meg, Candy, Mega, People and Seventeen. According to her, she was discovered by a talent scout when she accidentally walked into a shop while a shoot was ongoing. After a year she was brought to [[ABS-CBN]], Tried out a VTR with [[Star Magic]], and got a call back after a month. Eventually she qualified for Star Magic Batch 15. Collins was just 13 when she was launched as a Star Magic Batch 15 member. Under her stage name '''Isabelle Abiera''', she did small roles in ABS-CBN's ''[[Star Magic Presents]]: [[Astigs]]'' and ''Star Magic Presents: [[Abt Ur Luv|Abt Ur Luv Ur Lyf 2]]'' She also had a short hosting stint in [[Channel V]]. However, her entertainment career was put on a hold when she left for the United States. She was endorser of [[Sunsilk|SunSilk Co-Creations]] in 2010 along with [[Shaina Magdayao]], [[Nikki Gil]] and [[Sam Pinto]]. Collins made a comeback into the Philippine entertainment industry as one of the regular hosts of the defunct noontime program ''[[Wowowee]]'', at the same time she appeared as Veronica in the afternoon TV series ''[[Rosalka]]''. She played a planted [[gate-crashing|gate crasher]] in ''[[Pinoy Big Brother: Teen Clash 2010]]''. When ''Rosalka'' ended, she went on to play Christy in ''[[Precious Hearts Romances Presents]]: [[Alyna (TV series)|Alyna]]''. ===2011–present: Transfer to GMA Network=== [[File:Max Collins in 2023 Metro Manila Film Festival Parade of Stars (Firefly).png|thumb|upright=0.85|Collins at the [[2023 Metro Manila Film Festival]] parade of stars]] In 2010, when her contract with Star Magic ended, Collins left for the United States to "figure things out". A year after, she returned to the Philippines to relaunch her entertainment career. She changed her agent to Perry Lansigan's PPL Entertainment, Inc., changed her [[stage name]] to Max Collins, and finally signed an exclusive contract with [[GMA Network]]. In 2012, she starred as a supporting role in her first afternoon series project under [[GMA Network]], ''[[The Good Daughter]]'' and plays as Bea's ([[Kylie Padilla]]) best friend and a secret lover of Darwin. She also appeared in some episodes of ''[[Maynila (TV series)|Maynila]]''. She also starred in Primetime TV series ''[[Pahiram ng Sandali]]'' with Dingdong Dantes, alongside Lorna Tolentino and Boyet de Leon. In March 2015, Collins appeared as a cover girl for ''[[FHM Philippines]]''{{'}}s 15th anniversary issue, which she co-headlined with [[Tricia Santos (volleyball)|Tricia Santos]] and [[PBA on Sports5|PBA courtside reporter]] Rizza Diaz. Collins was included on the top 10 of the 2015 FHM 100 Sexiest Woman, Collins was on the ninth spot. ==Personal life== Collins is a cousin of actresses [[Lauren Young]] and [[Megan Young]]. '''Michael Francis Seander''' (born October 30, 1988), known professionally as '''Mike''' (stylized as '''mike.'''; formerly '''Mike Stud'''), is an American rapper, singer and former baseball player. His first musical recognition came with the release of his viral single "College Humor", which he recorded on [[GarageBand]] ironically<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/meet-mike-stud-college-baseball-player-turned-professional-bro-rapper/ |title= Meet Mike Stud, College Baseball Player Turned Professional Rapper |work= Vice |date=2013-04-10}}</ref> while he was a relief pitcher at [[Duke University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url = http://www.mstarz.com/articles/33249/20140707/former-college-baseball-prospect-mike-stud-who-suffered-tommy-john-surgery-releases-album-closer.htm|title = Former College Baseball Prospect Mike Stud Who Suffered Tommy John surgery Releases Album 'Closer'|last = Brown|first = Kenneth|date = July 7, 2014|work = Mstarz|access-date = August 6, 2015|archive-date = November 18, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151118192210/http://www.mstarz.com/articles/33249/20140707/former-college-baseball-prospect-mike-stud-who-suffered-tommy-john-surgery-releases-album-closer.htm|url-status = dead}}</ref>

== Early life ==
In 2006, Seander graduated from [[St. Raphael Academy]] in [[Pawtucket, Rhode Island]].  At {{convert|6|ft|2|in|abbr=on}}, he [[varsity letter|lettered]] in both baseball and basketball and was named Rhode Island's 2006 Gatorade Player of the Year, earning him an athletic scholarship to Duke University.<ref name="auto">{{cite web |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22847&SPID=1850&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=273422 |title= Duke Baseball Announces 2006 Signing Class |website= goduke.com |publisher= Duke University Athletics |date= 2006-05-03}}</ref> Seander earned 2nd team all-state honors in basketball after averaging 21 points and 7 rebounds as a senior. He earned an 8-2 record with a 0.72 ERA and 88 strikeouts for the Saints as a junior. In his senior season, he posted a 9-2 record, an ERA of 0.91, and struck out 107 en route to being named both the Gatorade Player of the Year<ref>{{cite web|url=http://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/archive.aspx |title=Gatorade POY archive |website=Gatorade.com |access-date=2013-02-15 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121227083536/http://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/archive.aspx |archive-date=2012-12-27 }}</ref> and Louisville Slugger Player of the Year in Rhode Island.<ref name="auto"/>

==Baseball career==
===Duke===
Seander attended [[Duke University]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]], to play baseball for the [[Duke Blue Devils baseball|Blue Devils]]. While at Duke, he was teammates with pitcher [[Marcus Stroman]], who would later appear on the remix of the title track of Seander's 2016 album ''These Days''.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nightengale |first1=Bob |title=Marcus Stroman's vision for life beyond baseball: 'I want a lane in everything' |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/mlb/2016/02/09/marcus-stroman-blue-jays-hdmh/80042990/ |access-date=July 14, 2019 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=February 10, 2016 |language=en}}</ref> In 2007, Seander saved nine games in 28 appearances and earned a 1.61 ERA (lowest in Duke University baseball history).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goduke.com/fls/4200/web-docs/2012%20Duke%20Baseball%20Media%20Guide.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=4200 |title= Duke Baseball Media Guide |format=PDF|website=Goduke.com}}</ref> Those nine saves were the fifth highest total in school history and was good for fourth best in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] that season. At season's end, Seander was named to the Louisville Slugger and Rivals.com Freshman All-American teams. The Rhode Island native also spent a summer in 2007 as the closer for the [[Newport Gulls]] in the [[NECBL]].<ref>{{cite web |title=A Stud Before Stud |url=https://pointstreak.com/news_story.html?id=533102|website=pointstreak.com |access-date=18 April 2024}}</ref> In 2008, Seander pitched in just three games due to elbow tendinitis and went 2–0 with a 4.05 ERA in 6 {{frac|2|3}} innings pitched. The injury would later require [[Tommy John surgery]]. In the summer, he pitched for the [[Wareham Gatemen]] of the [[Cape Cod League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Gatemen closer hopes it's his time  |url=https://www.southcoasttoday.com/story/sports/2008/06/15/gatemen-closer-hopes-it-s/52376117007/ |website=southcoasttoday.com |access-date=18 April 2024}}</ref> After missing the entire 2009 season recovering from the surgery, Seander appeared on the ACC Academic Honor Roll for the second year. In 2010, he appeared in nine games for the Blue Devils, striking out nine in  8{{frac|2|3}} innings pitched.<ref>{{cite web |title=2010 Baseball Roster Michael Seander  |url=https://goduke.com/sports/baseball/roster/michael-seander/5172 |website=goduke.com |access-date=18 April 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2011 Baseball Roster Michael Seander  |url=https://guhoyas.com/sports/baseball/roster/michael-seander/296 |website=guhoyas.com |access-date=18 April 2024}}</ref>

===Georgetown===
In 2010, Seander transferred to [[Georgetown University]] in [[Washington, D.C.]] to play for the [[Georgetown Hoyas baseball|Hoyas]]. In 21 appearances, he held a 4.29 ERA with 16 strikeouts and one save in 21 innings of work.<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Seander Player Stats |url=https://www.thebaseballcube.com/content/player/24733/ |website=thebaseballcube.com |access-date=18 April 2024}}</ref> He earned a graduate degree in sports management.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/dcsportsbog/2010/10/charlie_hustle_n_flow_hoyas_ba.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102095108/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/dcsportsbog/2010/10/charlie_hustle_n_flow_hoyas_ba.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 2, 2012 |title= Charlie Hustle 'n' Flow? Hoyas ballplayer records hip-hop tunes |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=2010-10-28}}</ref>

== Music career==
While recovering from surgery, Stud turned to music to pass the time.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mtv.com/news/1857068/mike-stud-closer-video/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140701032138/http://www.mtv.com/news/1857068/mike-stud-closer-video/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 1, 2014 |title=Mike Stud Gets One Step 'Closer' To His Dreams In New Video|website=Mtv.com|access-date=2015-08-05}}</ref>

In December 2010, Stud released a music video for "College Humor".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.startribune.com/big-gigs-jackson-browne-gov-t-mule-black-flag-keyshia-cole-warped-tour-more/267539631/ |title=Big Gigs: Jackson Browne, Gov't Mule, Black Flag, Keyshia Cole, Warped Tour, more |website=StarTribune.com |date=18 July 2014 |access-date=2015-08-05}}</ref> Stud stated that he originally made the track as a joke for his baseball teammates. Since its release, the video has been viewed over 2.5 million times (as of April 2021). In March, Stud followed up his hit with "In This Life", which featured West Coast rapper [[Alex Lagemann]].

All three hits were featured on Stud's first mixtape—''A Toast to Tommy''—which he released in October 2011.{{citation needed|date=August 2015}} In August, Stud released another mixtape, ''Click'', as a collaboration with fellow hip-hop artist Huey Mack.{{citation needed|date=August 2015}}

On May 13, 2013, Stud released his debut studio album ''[[Relief (Mike Stud album)|Relief]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mike.space/|title=4 The Homies Album Announcement and Member Signup|website=Mike.space|date=August 2015}}</ref>

On July 7, 2014, he released his second album ''[[Closer (Mike Stud album)|Closer]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6187756/mike-stud-number-one-album-closer-for-300-entertainment|title=Baseballer-Turned-Rapper Mike Stud Hits a Home Run With His No. 1 Album 'Closer'|website=Billboard.com |date=25 July 2014|access-date=2015-08-05}}</ref>

On October 30, 2015, he released an 8-track mini-album, ''This Isn't the Album'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fistintheair.com/2015/10/30/mike-stud-celebrates-birthday-with-release-of-this-isnt-the-album/|title=Mike Stud Celebrates Birthday with Release of 'This Isn't The Album'|website=Fistintheair.com|access-date=2015-10-30|archive-date=2015-11-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151101134350/http://fistintheair.com/2015/10/30/mike-stud-celebrates-birthday-with-release-of-this-isnt-the-album/|url-status=dead}}</ref> a mix of previously released singles and new tracks.

On January 12, 2016, Stud released his third studio album, ''These Days'', which includes a feature from former [[Toronto Blue Jays]] pitcher and former Duke teammate, [[Marcus Stroman]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://goodmusicallday.com/2016/01/mike-stud-tops-charts-new-album-thesedays-review/|title=Mike Stud Tops The Charts With New Project #TheseDays [Album Review] - GoodMusicAllDay|date=January 15, 2016}}</ref>

Mike most recently starred in a TV show on the Esquire Network called ''This Is Mike Stud''. The show follows him and his crew around on his most recent Back2YouTour. The show premiered Tuesday, June 21, 2016.

In 2017, Stud was featured on "To the Grave" by American singer-songwriter [[Bea Miller]], which is included on her EP, ''[[Chapter Three: Yellow]]'' and her second studio album, ''Aurora''.

On November 12, 2018, Stud released his fourth album, ''4TheHomies'', which included 23 songs and features from [[Vory (musician)|Vory]] and [[Goody Grace]]. The album is very special to Stud, as the pinned tweet reads, "Hey guys. I released a new project last night. 23 songs that are basically the last 2 years of my life in music form. I made every song in my house. this shit couldn't be more me. I hope u guys have as much fun listening as we did making it."

In 2018, Stud began his Final Mike Stud Tour, leading many fans to believe it was his last tour ever. However, he clarified this by saying he was merely changing his stage name to "Mike" after the tour concluded.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://us.blastingnews.com/showbiz-tv/2018/11/mike-stud-drops-new-album-4thehomies-002774477.html#:~:text=He%20has%20named%20his%20tour,his%20upcoming%20tour%20is%20done.|title = Mike Stud drops new album 4Thehomies|date = 15 November 2018}}</ref>

In 2021, the highs., was mike.'s first album released under his new stage name.

In 2022, mike. released “Why Not Us?” in collaboration with Skeez. 

In 2023, mike. released EP "Love," on Valentines Day.

In 2024, mike. released “the lows.” the second album in a series that will be concluded with “the inbetweens.”

'''Amanda Michelle Jiroux''' (born December 15, 1987), known professionally as '''Mandy Jiroux''', is an American singer, dancer, actress, choreographer, and DJ. She is known for co-developing ''The Miley and Mandy Show'' [[web series]] with [[Miley Cyrus]], and for her dance tutorial YouTube channel.<ref name="refinery">Todd, Carolyn L. (3/24/16). [http://www.refinery29.com/2016/03/106707/miley-cyrus-mandy-jiroux-youtube-show#slide Refinery29 – Revisiting The Miley & Mandy Show — & What The Hell Happened To Mandy]. Refinery29.com. Retrieved 2 November 2016.</ref><ref name="iHeart">Mastrogiannis, Nicole (8/11/16). [http://www.iheart.com/news/interview-mandy-jiroux-talks-new-single-15000941/ iHeart Radio interview] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023145531/http://www.iheart.com/news/interview-mandy-jiroux-talks-new-single-15000941/ |date=October 23, 2016 }}. Iheart.com. Retrieved 2 November 2016.</ref>

== Career ==
=== Choreography and backup dancing ===
Jiroux began dancing competitively by the age of 3 and toured with professional choreographers throughout her school years.<ref name="livingly">Rabinovitch, Simona (12/11/14). [http://www.livingly.com/Health+Diet+Fitness/articles/QKoOe5zmR8R/What+s+Her+Secret+Mandy+Jiroux Livingly – What's Her Secret: Mandy Jiroux]. Livingly.com. Retrieved 2 November 2016.</ref>

From 2007 to 2008, Jiroux served as a backup dancer for Miley Cyrus on her [[Best of Both Worlds Tour (Miley Cyrus)|Best of Both Worlds Tour]], and the two girls became friends. In 2008, they began ''The Miley and Mandy Show'' on YouTube, and their videos quickly accumulated millions of views.<ref name="blogtalk">Williams, Candace (4/15/09). [http://blog.blogtalkradio.com/blogtalkradio/miley-cyrus-bff-mandy-jiroux-our-age-difference-is-not-an-issue-but-i-am-a-better-burper-than-she-is/ Miley Cyrus’ BFF Mandy Jiroux: Our Age Difference Is NOT an Issue (but I AM a Better Burper Than She Is)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807102144/https://blog.blogtalkradio.com/blogtalkradio/miley-cyrus-bff-mandy-jiroux-our-age-difference-is-not-an-issue-but-i-am-a-better-burper-than-she-is/ |date=August 7, 2020 }}. blog.blogtalkradio.com. Retrieved 3 November 2016.</ref> She has later claimed that, during this period, Jiroux taught Cyrus how to [[twerk]].<ref name="lifestyle">Maycock, Selina (9/26/14). [http://lifestyle.one/heat/celebrity/news/didn-t-get-sing-wear-wanted-kris-jenner-s-girl-group-says-miley-cyrus-bff-mandy/ ‘I didn’t get to sing or wear what I wanted when I was in Kris Jenner’s girl group’ says Miley Cyrus’ BFF Mandy]. lifestyle.one. Retrieved 3 November 2016.</ref>

In April 2008, director [[Jon Chu]] and dancer [[Adam Sevani]] founded the ACDC Dance Cru and challenged Cyrus and Jiroux's "M&M Cru" to a YouTube dance competition.<ref name="NYTimes">(6/25/10). [https://www.nytimes.com/2010/06/25/arts/dance/25webdance.html?_r=0 It’s a Bird! It’s a Plane! No, It’s a Superdancer!]. nytimes.com. Retrieved 4 November 2016.</ref> The two crews continued to release dance videos over the following months, accumulating millions of views, and culminating in a final televised dance battle at the 2008 [[Teen Choice Awards]].<ref name="wired">Watercutter, Angela (8/04/08). [https://www.wired.com/2008/08/interview-membe/ M&M Cru, ACDC Take YouTube Dance Battle to Prime Time]. wired.com. Retrieved 4 November 2016.</ref>

=== With BG5 ===
[[File:Da Gurlz.jpg|thumb|right|Jiroux (second from left) with BG5 in 2009.]]
{{Main|YLA (group)|l1 =  BG5}}
In 2008, Jiroux joined the all-girl group [[YLA (group)|BG5]] (which stands for The Beach Girl5) alongside [[Brooke Allison]], Noreen Juliano, Laura New, and Dominique Domingo.<ref name="celebuzz">(9/27/10). [http://www.celebuzz.com/2010-09-27/five-things-you-need-to-know-about-bg5/ Five Things You Need to Know About BG5] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120427022625/http://www.celebuzz.com/2010-09-27/five-things-you-need-to-know-about-bg5/ |date=April 27, 2012 }}. celebuzz.com. Retrieved 3 November 2016.</ref> In 2010, [[Kris Jenner]] became part of the group's management and the group appeared in several episodes of ''[[Keeping Up with the Kardashians]]''.<ref name="lifestyle" /><ref name="celebuzz" /> The group opened for Justin Bieber and [[Selena Gomez]]; they also released an EP and several singles produced by [[Rock Mafia]].<ref name="celebuzz" />

Jiroux departed from the group in late 2012, citing a desire for more creative control over her music and style.<ref name="lifestyle" /> In 2014, she noted: "As much as I loved it and I loved the girls, I’m much happier doing my own thing."<ref name="lifestyle" />

=== Solo career ===

Jiroux continued a YouTube presence on her own channel dedicated to breaking down popular choreography into quick lessons. The [[web series|series]] has amassed millions of views, and her channel has over one million subscribers.<ref name="iHeart" /> In 2014, Jiroux partnered with YouTube musicians [[Chester See]] and [[Kurt Hugo Schneider]] to release a medley music video of [[Zedd]] songs.<ref name="j14">Van De Wall, Virginia (6/12/14). [http://www.j-14.com/posts/find-out-what-mandy-jiroux-from-the-miley-and-mandy-show-is-doing-now-39271/photos/miley-and-mandy-1-42613 Find Out What Mandy Jiroux From the 'Miley and Mandy Show' Is Doing Now] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160402170751/http://www.j-14.com/posts/find-out-what-mandy-jiroux-from-the-miley-and-mandy-show-is-doing-now-39271/photos/miley-and-mandy-1-42613 |date=April 2, 2016 }}. J-14.com. Retrieved 3 November 2016.</ref>

That same year, Jiroux DJed and performed at the Milwaukee Summerfest, in a lineup that included [[DJ Cassidy]] and [[Arctic Monkeys]].<ref name="tapmilwaukee">(7/05/14). [http://archive.jsonline.com/entertainment/festivals/complete-summerfest-2014-schedule-b99282613z1-261828101.html Complete Summerfest 2014 schedule]. jsonline.com. Retrieved 4 November 2016.</ref> Also in 2014, Jiroux was featured on "Tonight", a track by Fagault & Marina. The song was later remixed by DJ and EDM producer [[Starkillers]].<ref name="tapsongz">(7/16/14). [http://www.tapsongz.com/mandy-jiroux after performance at summerfest, mandy jiroux prepares new releases]. tapsongz.com. Retrieved 4 November 2016.</ref><ref name="thatdrop">(7/29/14). [http://www.thatdrop.com/starkillers-premiere-remix-tonight-fagault-marina-ft-mandy-jiroux/ Starkillers Premiere Remix of “Tonight” by Fagault & Marina ft. Mandy Jiroux]. Thatdrop.com. Retrieved 7 November 2016.</ref>

In 2015, Jiroux released the single "My Forever", under VarCity Productions, which was followed by "Fade Away" the next year, under [[Armada Music]].<ref name="powerhouse">(7/17/15). [http://www.powerhousemusic.nl/releases/mandy-jiroux-feat-reez-my-forever/ Mandy Jiroux ft. Reez – My Forever]{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}. powerhousemusic.nl. Retrieved 7 November 2016.</ref> Both tracks were collaborations with EDM duo REEZ.<ref name="housem">(1/18/16). [http://www.housem.nl/2016/01/18/reez-teams-up-with-mandy-jiroux/ REEZ TEAMS UP WITH MANDY JIROUX]. housem.nl. Retrieved 4 November 2016.</ref>

In 2016, Jiroux was sued by members of the band [[Blind Melon]] over her song "Insane", which incorporated large sections of Blind Melon's "[[No Rain]]".<ref>[https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/blind-melon-sues-insane-songwriters-923580 Blind Melon Sues "Insane" Songwriters for Covering Up 'No Rain' Infringement], The Hollywood Reporter (Aug. 30, 2016)</ref> According to the lawsuit, Blind Melon's manager and guitarist were told by Mandy's manager that "Insane" was merely a cover of "No Rain", but upon discovering the liberties that "Insane" took with the original song, concluded that it was actually a "derivative work" under copyright law and consequently unauthorized. The lawsuit was settled between the parties the following year.<ref>[https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/blind-melon-settles-insane-copyright-lawsuit-973828 Blind Melon Settles "Insane" Copyright Lawsuit], The Hollywood Reporter (Feb. 9, 2017)</ref>

'''Phillip Chijoke Ejimadu''' (born August 31, 1999) is an American [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for the [[Kansas City Comets (2010–)|Kansas City Comets]] in the [[Major Arena Soccer League]].

== Career ==
=== Club ===
Ejimadu played in the youth academy of [[Nacional Atlético Clube (SP)|Nacional Atlético Clube]] in [[São Paulo]], [[Brazil]] before returning to the United States to go pro. He signed with [[Major League Soccer]] outfit, [[Los Angeles FC]] on February 21, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=LAFC Signs Phillip Ejimadu, Lamar Batista, & Adrien Perez Ahead Of 2019 Season |url=https://www.lafc.com/post/2019/02/21/lafc-signs-phillip-ejimadu-lamar-batista-adrien-perez-ahead-2019-season |website=lafc.com |accessdate=April 1, 2019}}</ref> On March 29, 2019, Ejimadu went on a season-long loan to third-division, [[FC Tucson]].<ref name="fc tucson loan">{{cite web |title=LAFC Loans Goalkeeper Phillip Ejimadu To FC Tucson |url=https://www.lafc.com/es/post/2019/03/29/lafc-loans-goalkeeper-phillip-ejimadu-fc-tucson |website=lafc.com |accessdate=April 1, 2019}}</ref> The next day, Ejimadu made his professional debut for FC Tucson starting the entire match in a 3–1 victory at [[Orlando City B]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Orlando City B v FC Tucson |url=https://www.uslleagueone.com/orlandocityb-fctucson-1035085 |website=[[USL League One]] |accessdate=April 1, 2019}}</ref>

On September 23, 2020, Ejimadu moved on loan to [[USL Championship]] side [[San Diego Loyal SC|San Diego Loyal]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lafc.com/news/lafc-loans-goalkeeper-phillip-ejimadu-san-diego-loyal-sc|title=LAFC Loans Goalkeeper Phillip Ejimadu To San Diego Loyal SC | Los Angeles Football Club|website=LAFC}}</ref>

On April 5, 2021, Ejimadu joined [[Las Vegas Lights FC]] ahead of the 2021 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=LIGHTS FC ANNOUNCE INITIAL SET OF PLAYER SIGNINGS FOR 2021 SEASON|url=https://www.lasvegaslightsfc.com/news_article/show/1156231|publisher=Las Vegas Lights FC|access-date=April 5, 2021|archive-date=April 5, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210405170126/https://www.lasvegaslightsfc.com/news_article/show/1156231|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On March 13, 2022, Ejimadu signed with [[MLS Next Pro]] side [[Rochester New York FC]] for the 2022 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=x.com |url=https://x.com/rnyfcofficial/status/1503148076181172233 |access-date=June 17, 2024 |website=X (formerly Twitter)}}</ref>

Ejimadu signed with the [[Major Arena Soccer League]]'s [[Kansas City Comets (2010–)|Kansas City Comets]] on October 17, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dunn |first1=Nathan |title=COMETS SIGN GOALKEEPER PHILLIP EJIMADU |url=https://www.kccomets.com/news/comets-sign-goalkeeper-phillip-ejimadu |website=KCComets.com |publisher=[[Kansas City Comets (2010–)|Kansas City Comets]] |access-date=17 October 2023}}</ref>

=== International ===
Ejimadu is eligible to represent Brazil, Nigeria, and the United States on the international level.<ref>{{cite web |title=Phillip Ejimadu - LAFC - Goalkeeper |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/players/phillip-ejimadu |website=MLSSoccer.com |accessdate=April 2, 2019 |quote=The Minnesota-born player also holds Nigerian and Brazilian citizenship.}}</ref> In 2018, he was called into the training camp for the [[United States men's national under-20 soccer team|United States under-20]] national team.<ref name="fc tucson loan"/>
