'''Bethany Catherine Bos''' ({{née|'''Balcer'''}}; born March 7, 1997) is an American professional [[Association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]]. Bos played [[college soccer]] for the [[Spring Arbor Cougars women's soccer|Spring Arbor Cougars]], where she was a two-time [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] national champion, three-time [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] national player of the year, four-time first-team All-American, and the school's leading scorer.

After going undrafted, Bos signed with the [[Seattle Reign FC|Seattle Reign]], becoming the first NAIA player in the NWSL, and was named the [[NWSL Rookie of the Year]] in 2019. She spent five-and-a-half seasons with the Reign, winning the [[NWSL Shield]] in 2022, earning two [[NWSL Second XI]] selections, and becoming the club's [[List of Seattle Reign FC players|third all-time top scorer]]. She was traded to [[Racing Louisville FC|Racing Louisville]] in mid-2024. Bos signed with [[USL Super League]] club [[Dallas Trinity FC]] in 2026.

Bos earned one [[cap (association football)|cap]] with the [[United States women's national soccer team|United States national team]] in 2021.

==Early life==
Bos grew up in [[Hudsonville, Michigan]] and attended [[Unity Christian High School (Hudsonville)|Unity Christian High School]], where she played varsity soccer and basketball.<ref name="college">{{cite news |title=Balcer to Bring Attacking Skills to Lady Cougars in 2015 |url=https://www.saucougars.com/article/2983.php |access-date=April 13, 2019 |publisher=Spring Arbor Cougars |date=January 24, 2014 |archive-date=April 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413173928/https://www.saucougars.com/article/2983.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> She is the fourth of five children.{{Citation needed|date=December 2024}}

==College career==
Bos attended [[Spring Arbor University]] from 2015 to 2019, where she was a four-year starter on its varsity soccer team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bethany Balcer |url=https://www.saucougars.com/roster/16/13/4560.php |publisher=Spring Arbor Cougars |access-date=April 13, 2019 |archive-date=April 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413174054/https://www.saucougars.com/roster/16/13/4560.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Cougars advanced to the [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] Final Four every year and won two national titles with Bos on the team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bethany Balcer - 2018 - Women's Soccer |url=https://saucougars.com/sports/wsoc/roster/bethany-balcer/12496 |access-date=2025-02-21 |website=Spring Arbor University |language=en}}</ref> She was named the NAIA national player of the year three times and first-team All-American all four years.<ref name="nri"/>

While in college, Bos played as an amateur with senior teams over the summer. She led [[Grand Rapids FC (women)|Grand Rapids FC]] to a [[United Women's Soccer]] championship in 2017 – scoring hat-tricks in five straight matches – and played with [[Seattle Sounders Women]] in the [[Women's Premier Soccer League]] the following year winning the WPSL championship.<ref>{{cite news |title=Balcer seizing opportunity with Seattle Sounders Women |url=https://www.saucougars.com/article/5275.php |access-date=April 13, 2019 |publisher=Spring Arbor Cougars |date=June 12, 2018 |archive-date=April 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413173844/https://www.saucougars.com/article/5275.php |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Club career==
===Seattle Reign===
Bos was invited to the [[Reign FC]] preseason training camp prior to the [[2019 NWSL season]]<ref name="nri">{{cite news |title=Balcer Joins Reign FC for Preseason Camp |url=https://www.saucougars.com/article/5604.php |access-date=April 13, 2019 |publisher=Spring Arbor Cougars |date=March 7, 2019 |archive-date=April 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413173843/https://www.saucougars.com/article/5604.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> and subsequently earned a contract on the club's supplemental roster.<ref name="signing">{{cite news |title=Reign FC Announce Signing of Forward Bethany Balcer |url=https://www.reignfc.com/news/2019/4/13/reign-fc-announce-signing-of-forward-bethany-balcer |access-date=April 13, 2019 |publisher=Reign FC |date=April 13, 2019}}</ref> She was the first [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] player to sign with an [[NWSL]] club<ref>{{cite news |title=Balcer signs professional contract with NWSL's Reign FC |url=https://www.saucougars.com/article/5690.php |access-date=April 14, 2019 |publisher=Spring Arbor Cougars |date=April 14, 2019 |archive-date=April 14, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190414140850/https://www.saucougars.com/article/5690.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> and only the third NWSL player to previously play collegiately in the United States and finish their collegiate career with a non-[[NCAA Division I|NCAA D-I]] institution.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Henderson |first1=Chris |title=Pretty sure Francis Marion was still DI when Salem was there. Didn't even consider figuring in Canadian colleges (Robinson). Forgot all about Cordner and Pires. |url=https://twitter.com/chris_awk/status/1117102781913899008 |publisher=Twitter |access-date=April 14, 2019}}</ref> Bos made her NWSL debut coming on as an 86th-minute substitute at the [[Houston Dash]] on April 14, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cristobal |first1=Jacob |title=Reign FC open season with a draw at Houston Dash |url=https://www.sounderatheart.com/2019/4/14/18310673/reign-fc-houston-dash-recap-draw |publisher=Sounder at Heart |access-date=April 22, 2019 |date=April 14, 2019 |archive-date=July 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220705193651/https://www.sounderatheart.com/2019/4/14/18310673/reign-fc-houston-dash-recap-draw |url-status=dead }}</ref> A week later, she made her first start in Reign's home-opener at [[Cheney Stadium]]. Curling a shot from the edge of the penalty area into the far corner of the goal, she scored her first-ever pro goal in the 21st minute against [[Orlando Pride]] in a 1–1 tie. It was also the first home goal scored in the Reign's first season in [[Tacoma, Washington]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=VanDyke |first1=Josh |title=Bethany Balcer steps in for Olympian and scores first goal with Reign FC |url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/jackson/2019/04/bethany-balcer-scores-first-professional-goal-with-reign-fc.html |access-date=April 22, 2019 |work=MLive.com |date=April 22, 2019}}</ref>
She scored her second goal in her second home start, sixth appearance on May 27, 2019, in a 2–1 win against the defending champions [[North Carolina Courage]]. Her 13th-minute header from the edge of the box crashed off the underside of the bar to give her side an early lead. 
Her third goal occurred in the next game in her third home start against the Houston Dash. On a breakaway she picked up a deflected through ball from [[Darian Jenkins]] and slotted right-footed past the keeper for the first goal of the game in the 32nd minute, Houston tied in the 90th to split the points.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Reign FC Concedes Late Equalizer in Draw With Houston Dash |url=https://www.reignfc.com/news/2019/6/2/reign-fc-concedes-late-equalizer-in-draw-with-houston-dash-53yhy |access-date=2025-02-21 |website=Seattle Reign FC |language=en-US}}</ref> At the end of the season, she was awarded the 2019 [[NWSL Rookie of the Year|Rookie of the Year Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=NWSL |date=2019-10-29 |title=Reign FC forward Bethany Balcer named 2019 NWSL Rookie of the Year {{!}} National Women's Soccer League Official Site |url=https://www.nwslsoccer.com/news/reign-fc-forward-bethany-balcer-named-2019-nwsl-rookie-of-the-year |access-date=2025-02-21 |website=NWSL |language=en}}</ref>

Bos established herself as one of the Reign's leading players and was the club's top scorer every season she spent there.<ref name="JWS23">{{cite news|url=https://justwomenssports.com/reads/bethany-balcer-ol-reign-nwsl-goals-mental-health/|title=How Bethany Balcer became the NWSL's most unorthodox star|last=Watkins|first=Claire|date=2023-06-28|website=[[Just Women's Sports]]|access-date=2024-08-19}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Seattle Reign FC Stats and History |url=https://fbref.com/en/squads/257fad2b/history/Seattle-Reign-FC-Stats-and-History |work=[[FBref.com|FBref]] |publisher=[[Sports Reference]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240126041931/https://fbref.com/en/squads/257fad2b/history/Seattle-Reign-FC-Stats-and-History |archive-date=January 26, 2024 |accessdate=June 5, 2024}}</ref> She helped lead the Reign to top of the standings for the [[2022 National Women's Soccer League season|2022 season]], winning the [[NWSL Shield]].<ref name="JWS23"/> She scored 33 regular-season goals during her tenure with the Reign, the third-highest total in the NWSL from 2019 to mid-2024.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wdrb.com/sports/greever-racing-louisville-fc-pays-a-captains-price-in-an-attempt-to-make-a-needed/article_27ef76be-5eeb-11ef-a591-bf4281bd519b.html|title=Racing Louisville FC pays a captain's price in an attempt to make a needed playoff push|last=Greever|first=Tyler|date=2024-08-20|publisher=[[WDRB]]|access-date=2024-08-20}}</ref> Upon her departure, she was the Reign's [[List of Seattle Reign FC players|third-highest scorer]] in club history.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.racingloufc.com/news/2024/08/19/racing-louisville-trade-bethany-balcer/|title=Racing lands one of NWSL's top scorers in trade for Balcer|date=2024-08-19|publisher=[[Racing Louisville FC]]|access-date=2025-11-26}}</ref>

=== Racing Louisville===
[[File: 20250713 ctc 42625 copy.jpg|thumb|Bos with [[Racing Louisville FC|Racing Louisville]] in 2025|308x308px]]
On August 19, 2024, Bos was traded to [[Racing Louisville FC]] in exchange for [[Jaelin Howell]] and $50,000 in allocation money.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Reign FC Acquires Midfielder Jaelin Howell and Allocation Money in Trade with Racing Louisville FC |url=https://www.reignfc.com/news/seattle-reign-fc-acquires-midfielder-jaelin-howell-and-allocation-money-in-trade-with-racing-louisville-fc |access-date=2024-08-19 |website=Seattle Reign FC |language=en-US}}</ref> She made her Louisville debut five days later, starting in a match against the [[Chicago Red Stars]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Team News: Balcer set to start in debut |url=https://www.racingloufc.com/news/2024/08/24/team-news-bethany-balcer-set-to-start-in-debut/#:~:text=Will%20Carlon/Racing%20Louisville%20FC,to%20Utah%20on%20Friday%20night. |access-date=2025-02-21 |website=Racing Louisville FC |language=en-US}}</ref> She scored her first goal with the club in a comeback victory against [[Angel City FC]] on September 14, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Recap: Racing rallies for vital win |url=https://www.racingloufc.com/news/2024/09/14/recap-racing-rallies-for-vital-win/ |access-date=2025-02-21 |website=Racing Louisville FC |language=en-US}}</ref>

Bos announced that she would be taking a mental health leave away from the sport in March 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=Racing Louisville's Balcer taking break from soccer: 'Lost my joy' |date= March 19, 2025 |first= Jeff |last=Kassouf |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/44317072/racing-louisville-bethany-balcer-break-soccer-lost-joy |website=ESPN}}</ref> After returning to the pitch in August, Bos scored one goal before becoming a free agent at the end of the 2025 season. On November 26, 2025, Racing Louisville announced that Bos would not be re-signing with the team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Racing to bring back 17 players from 2025 playoff team |url=https://www.racingloufc.com/news/2025/11/26/racing-louisville-fc-end-of-season-roster-update-2025/ |website=Racing Louisville FC |access-date=November 27, 2025}}</ref>

=== Dallas Trinity ===

On February 3, 2026, [[USL Super League]] club [[Dallas Trinity FC]] announced that they had signed Bos midway through the [[2025–26 USL Super League season|2025–26 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dallas Trinity signs Bethany Bos (Balcer), one of the NWSL's top strikers |date= February 3, 2026 |first= Dennis |last= McGowan |website= 3rd Degree |url=https://3rddegree.net/dallas-trinity-sign-bethany-bos-balcer-one-of-the-nwsls-top-strikers?amp=1}}</ref> Bos made her Super League debut four days later, coming on as a second-half substitute for [[Camryn Lancaster]] in a 4–0 victory over [[Fort Lauderdale United FC]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-08 |title=Dallas Trinity FC Handles Fort Lauderdale United FC, 4-0 |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/dallas-trinity-fc-handles-fort-lauderdale-united-fc-4-0/n-6324357 |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=OurSports Central |language=en}}</ref> She went on to appear in every match for Dallas across the rest of the season, scoring three goals and helping the Trinity qualify for the playoffs for the second consecutive campaign.<ref name=":0">{{Cite Instagram |postid=DZLhbNRH9p9 |user=dallastrinityfc |title=@bethanybalcer stepped into the Cotton Bowl for the first time and immediately made an impact on the club. She featured in every match since joining the roster, contributing 3 goals, and brought experience, quality, and professionalism to the team every day. Thank you for all you've done. |author=Dallas Trinity FC |author-link=Dallas Trinity FC |date=June 4, 2026 |access-date=June 4, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=2026-05-23 |title=Dallas Trinity FC can't break through, falls to Lexington SC in the playoffs to end season |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/fc-dallas/article/dallas-trinity-fc-falls-lexington-sc-playoffs-22272234.php |access-date=2026-06-04 |newspaper=}}</ref> On June 4, 2026, the club announced that Bos would be departing from Dallas at the end of the season.<ref name=":0" />

==International career==
Bos received her first call-up to the [[United States women's national soccer team]] in December 2019.<ref>{{cite news |title=ANDONOVSKI NAMES 24-PLAYER ROSTER FOR U.S. WOMEN'S NATIONAL TEAM DECEMBER IDENTIFICATION TRAINING CAMP IN FLORIDA |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2019/11/andonovski-names-24-player-roster-for-uswnt-december-identification-training-camp-in-florida |access-date=28 November 2019 |publisher=US Soccer |date=27 November 2019}}</ref> She made her international debut on November 26, 2021, against [[Australia women's national soccer team|Australia]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Australia vs United States |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/competitions/uswnt-friendlies-2021/matches/australia-vs-united-states-11-26-2021 |access-date=27 November 2021 |publisher=US Soccer |date=26 November 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Australia vs USWNT Match Report |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2021/11/international-friendly-11-26-21-australia-vs-uswnt-match-report |access-date=27 November 2021 |publisher=US Soccer |date=27 November 2021}}</ref> She was previously a member of the [[United States women's national under-23 soccer team]].<ref>{{cite news |last=VanDyke |first=Josh |title=Bethany Balcer named to U.S. U-23 Women's National Team |url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/jackson/2019/08/bethany-balcer-named-to-us-u-23-womens-national-team.html |access-date=16 April 2023 |publisher=MLive.com |date=21 August 2019}}</ref>

==Style of play==

Bos plays as a [[striker (association football)|striker]]. She is known for her scoring ability off [[header (association football)|header]]s.<ref name="JWS23"/>

==Personal life==
Bos is a [[Christians|Christian]].<ref name="athletic_faith_seizing_opps">{{cite web |last1=Pentz |first1=Matt |title=Bethany Balcer's NWSL journey of faith, acceptance and seizing opportunities |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1902814/2020/06/30/bethany-balcers-nwsl-journey-of-faith-acceptance-and-seizing-opportunities/ |publisher=The Athletic |access-date=10 November 2021 |date=June 30, 2020}}</ref>
Her brother Nicholas is a soccer referee<ref name="balcer_earns_second_player_of_the_year">{{cite web |last1=Padilla |first1=Lenny |title=Bethany Balcer earns National Soccer Player of the Year for second time |url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/grand-rapids/2017/12/bethany_balcer_earns_national.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109034621/https://www.mlive.com/sports/grand-rapids/2017/12/bethany_balcer_earns_national.html |archive-date=November 9, 2020 |publisher=mLive |access-date=November 8, 2023 |date=December 6, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> who has worked for [[Professional Referee Organization|PRO]]<ref name="nicholas_balcer_pro">{{cite web |title=PRO2 Assistant Referees |website=PRO Referees |url=https://proreferees.com/roster/pro2-assistant-referees/ |access-date=December 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231110152533/https://proreferees.com/roster/pro2-assistant-referees/ |archive-date=November 10, 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> and the [[NCAA]].<ref name="nicholas_balcer_ncaa">{{cite web |url=https://clemsontigers.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/23-1201_ClemsonFloridaStateFinalStats.pdf |access-date=December 1, 2023 |title=Soccer Box Score (Final) 2023 NCAA Women's College Cup Clemson vs. Florida St. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231202020423/https://clemsontigers.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/23-1201_ClemsonFloridaStateFinalStats.pdf |archive-date=December 2, 2023 |url-status=live |website=[[Clemson Tigers]]}}</ref> and MLS. 
Her sister Shannon is the head woman's soccer coach at Spring Arbor University.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://saucougars.com/news/2024/1/22/andringa-takes-full-reins-of-sau-womens-soccer-program.aspx | title=Andringa takes full reins of SAU women's soccer program | date=January 22, 2024 }}</ref> She married Christian Bos on January 3, 2026 and subsequently began using her married name.

Miller made his international debut for [[Fiji national rugby league team|Fiji]] in their 56–14 victory vs [[Lebanon national rugby league team|Lebanon]] in the 2019 Pacific Test.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wwos.nine.com.au/nrl/live-scores/fiji-v-lebanon-international-2019/719011#lineup |title=Fiji vs Lebanon |publisher=Wide World of Sports |date=22 June 2019}}</ref>

'''Vergil Ortiz Jr.''' (born March 25, 1998) is an American [[professional boxer]]. He has held the [[World Boxing Council]] (WBC) [[interim championship|interim]] [[super welterweight]] title since 2024.

As an [[amateur boxing|amateur]], he was a seven-time national champion and won the 110 pounds category at the USA's Junior Olympic National Championships in 2013.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.goldenboypromotions.com/en/fighter/vergil-ortiz-jr|title=Vergil Ortiz Jr Golden Boy Promotions|work=goldenboypromotions.com|access-date=21 September 2019|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usaboxing.org/results/2013/june/26/2013-junior-olympic-national-championships |title=2013 Junior Olympic National Championships }}</ref> He was named the 2019 [[The Ring magazine Prospect of the Year|Prospect of the Year]] by ''[[The Ring (magazine)|The Ring]]'' magazine.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Prospect of the Year|url=https://www.ringtv.com/article/2019prospect-2/|access-date=2021-06-12|website=The Ring}}</ref> Ortiz is known for his exceptional punching power, having scored all but two of his wins by [[knockout]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=BoxRec: Vergil Ortiz Jr|url=https://boxrec.com/en/box-pro/766727|access-date=2021-06-12|archive-date=July 23, 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190723223409/https://boxrec.com/en/proboxer/766727|website=boxrec.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Early career===
Ortiz was victorious in his first six fights, winning all six by stoppage and only going past the first round in one of the six fights.

====Ortiz Jr vs. Valenzuela====
His seventh bout came on September 16, 2017, on the undercard of [[Canelo Álvarez vs. Gennady Golovkin|Canelo Álvarez vs. Gennady Golovkin I]] against Cesar Valenzuela, which he won by second-round technical knockout.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vergil Ortiz Jr. vs. Cesar Valenzuela, GGG vs. Canelo {{!}} Boxing Bout|url=https://www.tapology.com/fightcenter/bouts/499542-ggg-vs-canelo-vergil-ortiz-jr-vs-cesar-valenzuela|access-date=2021-06-12|website=Tapology|language=en}}</ref>

====Ortiz Jr vs. Ortiz====
After improving to 11-0, Ortiz appeared a year later on the undercard of [[Canelo Álvarez vs. Gennady Golovkin II]] to face [[Roberto Ortiz (boxer)|Roberto Ortiz]]. Vergil Ortiz knocked down his opponent with a right hand early in the second round. Roberto got up, but he was still hurt. Vergil attacked him immediately and knocked him down again with a right hand that sent his opponent to one knee. Roberto Ortiz reached his feet again, but the referee deemed him unfit to continue, calling off the fight.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Idec|first=Keith|title=Vergil Ortiz Stops Roberto Ortiz In Two on Canelo-GGG Card|url=https://www.boxingscene.com/vergil-ortiz-stops-roberto-ortiz-two-on-canelo-ggg-card--131860|access-date=2021-06-12|website=BoxingScene.com|date=September 15, 2018 |language=en-us}}</ref>

===Rise up the ranks===

====Ortiz Jr vs. Orozco====
Ortiz, who now had an unblemished record of 13-0, defeated [[Antonio Orozco (boxer)|Antonio Orozco]] by sixth-round technical knockout to win the vacant [[World Boxing Association|WBA Gold]] welterweight title on August 10, 2019, at [[The Theatre at Grand Prairie]], Texas.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Christ|first=Scott|date=2019-08-10|title=Vergil Ortiz Jr stops Orozco in six, Franco and Negrete draw again|url=https://www.badlefthook.com/2019/8/10/20800358/ortiz-vs-orozco-results-stoppage-sixth-round-franco-negrete-3-draw-dazn-boxing|access-date=2021-04-28|website=Bad Left Hook|language=en}}</ref> He defended the title in his next fight against [[Brad Solomon]] on December 13, 2019, in [[Indio, California|Indio]], California, winning by fifth-round knockout.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vergil Ortiz Jr. records fifth-round KO of Brad Solomon for 15th victory {{!}} DAZN News US|url=https://www.dazn.com/en-US/news/boxing/vergil-ortiz-jr-records-fifth-round-ko-of-brad-solomon-for-15th-victory/1w0a2epihiann1llczv27fuhni|access-date=2021-04-28|website=DAZN|date=December 14, 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

====Ortiz Jr vs. Vargas====
Ortiz was originally [[Vergil Ortiz Jr. vs. Samuel Vargas|scheduled to face Samuel Vargas]] on March 28, 2020, at [[The Forum (Inglewood, California)|The Forum]], [[Inglewood, California|Inglewood]], California on the undercard of [[Canelo Álvarez vs. Billy Joe Saunders]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-03-01|title=Canelo's coach confirms Saunders next for Mexican superstar|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/boxing/canelo-alvarez-next-fight-billy-joe-saunders-callum-smith-opponent-a9367046.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220811/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/boxing/canelo-alvarez-next-fight-billy-joe-saunders-callum-smith-opponent-a9367046.html |archive-date=August 11, 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|access-date=2021-04-28|website=The Independent|language=en}}</ref> However, following the postponement of the fight between Álvarez and Saunders due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the fight took place on July 24, 2020, at the same venue as Ortiz's previous fight against Brad Solomon.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-06-30|title=BOXING IS BACK ON DAZN|url=https://media.dazn.com/en/press-releases/2020/06/boxing-is-back-on-dazn/|access-date=2021-04-28|website=DAZN Media Centre|language=en-GB|archive-date=July 20, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200720201011/https://media.dazn.com/en/press-releases/2020/06/boxing-is-back-on-dazn/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Ortiz won the fight by seventh-round technical knockout and retained his WBA Gold welterweight title.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ortiz vs. Vargas results: Vergil Ortiz Jr. pummels Samuel Vargas to notch 16th consecutive KO {{!}} DAZN News UK|url=https://www.dazn.com/en-GB/news/boxing/vergil-ortiz-jr-vs-samuel-vargas-live-results-updates-highlights/1fjo8x6u1xehp1t2f1y1ibh7no|access-date=2021-04-28|website=DAZN|date=July 25, 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

====Ortiz Jr vs. Hooker====
Ortiz returned to the ring on March 20, 2021, beating [[Maurice Hooker]] with another seventh-round technical knockout in [[Fort Worth, Texas|Fort Worth]], Texas to win the vacant [[World Boxing Organization|WBO]] International welterweight title.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Christ|first=Scott|date=2021-03-21|title=Results and highlights: Vergil Ortiz Jr stops Maurice Hooker in firefight, Seniesa Estrada wins first world title|url=https://www.badlefthook.com/2021/3/21/22342318/ortiz-vs-hooker-results-highlights-vergil-stops-maurice-seniesa-estrada-dazn-boxing-news-2021|access-date=2021-04-28|website=Bad Left Hook|language=en}}</ref> Hooker was ranked #8 by the WBO, #13 by the WBC and #15 by the IBF at welterweight.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ortiz Jr vs Hooker - News, Tape, Ringwalk, TV, Streaming & Tickets |url=https://box.live/fights/ortiz-jr-vs-hooker/ |access-date=2022-08-11 |website=Box.Live |language=en-US}}</ref>

====Ortiz Jr vs. Kavaliauskas====
On August 14, 2021, Ortiz defended the title against [[Egidijus Kavaliauskas]]. Kavaliauskas was ranked #5 by the WBO and #10 by the WBC at welterweight.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zamarripa |first=Jaime |title=Ortiz Jr vs Kavaliauskas - News, Tape, Ringwalk, TV, Streaming & Tickets |url=https://box.live/fights/ortiz-jr-vs-kavaliauskas/ |access-date=2022-08-11 |website=Box.Live |language=en-US}}</ref> Kavaliauskas, who became Ortiz's first opponent to last longer than seven rounds, suffered five knockdowns as Ortiz won by eighth-round technical knockout.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vergil Ortiz Jr. overcomes adversity to knock down Mean Machine five times to win by eighth-round TKO {{!}} DAZN News US|url=https://www.dazn.com/en-US/news/boxing/vergil-ortiz-jr-vs-mean-machine-live-updates-results-highlights-from-full-card/1o69e3xznb9iq17e9z4nuoak3t|access-date=2021-08-15|website=DAZN|date=August 15, 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

====Ortiz Jr vs. McKinson====
On August 6, 2022, Ortiz Jr fought [[Michael McKinson]] in an eliminator for the WBA world welterweight title. McKinson was ranked #5 by the WBO and #10 by the WBA at welterweight. Ortiz Jr beat McKinson by technical knockout in the 9th round.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ericna |title=Ortiz Jr vs McKinson - News, Tape, Ringwalk, TV, Streaming & Tickets |url=https://box.live/fights/ortiz-jr-vs-mckinson/ |access-date=2022-08-11 |website=Box.Live |language=en-US}}</ref>

====Ortiz Jr vs. Dulorme====
On April 27, 2024 in Fresno, CA, Ortiz Jr was scheduled to face [[Thomas Dulorme]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Iskenderov |first1=Parviz |title=Vergil Ortiz Jr vs Thomas Dulorme co-feature to Ramirez-Barthelemy |url=https://www.fightmag.com/vergil-ortiz-jr-vs-thomas-dulorme-co-feature-to-ramirez-barthelemy/ |work=FIGHTMAG |date=27 March 2024}}</ref> He won the fight by knockout with liver shot in the first round.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Iskenderov |first1=Parviz |title=Vergil Ortiz Jr KO's Thomas Dulorme in first round, 'ready' for Tim Tszyu |url=https://www.fightmag.com/vergil-ortiz-jr-kos-thomas-dulorme-in-first-round-ready-for-tim-tszyu/ |work=FIGHTMAG |date=28 April 2024}}</ref>

====Ortiz Jr vs. Tszyu====
Ortiz Jr was scheduled to face [[Tim Tszyu]] on August 3, 2024 at [[BMO Stadium]] in Los Angeles.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Iskenderov |first1=Parviz |title=Tim Tszyu to face Vergil Ortiz Jr on Crawford vs Madrimov card in LA |url=https://www.fightmag.com/tim-tszyu-to-face-vergil-ortiz-jr-on-crawford-vs-madrimov-card-in-la/ |work=FIGHTMAG |date=25 April 2024}}</ref> On May 30, 2024 it was announced that the fight was canceled with medical advice.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Iskenderov |first1=Parviz |title=Tim Tszyu vs Vergil Ortiz Jr fight canceled on medical advice |url=https://www.fightmag.com/tim-tszyu-vs-vergil-ortiz-jr-fight-canceled-on-medical-advice/ |work=FIGHTMAG |date=31 May 2024}}</ref> Tszyu required more time to heal from the injury sustained in his previous bout against Sebastian Fundora in March.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tsyzu-Ortiz bout cancelled on medical advice |url=https://www.espn.com.au/boxing/story/_/id/40248046/boxing-tim-tszyu-vs-vergil-ortiz-fight-cancelled |work=ESPN.com |date=31 May 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

===Interim WBC super welterweight champion===
====Ortiz Jr vs. Bohachuk====
On June 24, 2024 it was announced that Ortiz Jr would face [[Serhii Bohachuk]] in Las Vegas on August 10, 2024.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sources: Ortiz, Bohachuk agree to fight in Vegas |url=https://www.espn.com/boxing/story/_/id/40421757/ortiz-bohachuk-agree-aug-10-fight-las-vegas |work=ESPN.com |date=24 June 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Iskenderov |first1=Parviz |title=Vergil Ortiz Jr to face Serhii Bohachuk in Las Vegas in August |url=https://www.fightmag.com/vergil-ortiz-jr-to-face-serhii-bohachuk-in-las-vegas-in-august/ |work=FIGHTMAG |date=25 June 2024}}</ref> Ortiz was knocked down twice in the bout, but went on to win via majority decision (114–112, 114–112, 113–113) after twelve competitive rounds;<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-11 |title=Vergil Ortiz Jr. outlasts Serhii Bohachuk for majority decision win in Fight of the Year contender |url=https://www.cbssports.com/boxing/news/vergil-ortiz-jr-outlasts-serhii-bohachuk-for-majority-decision-win-in-fight-of-the-year-contender/ |access-date=2024-08-20 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> this being the first time Ortiz had gone the full distance in a fight.

====Ortiz Jr vs. Madrimov====
On February 22, 2025 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Ortiz Jr defeated [[Israil Madrimov]] by unanimous decision to retain his interim WBC super welterweight title, with two scores reading 115–113 and one reading 117–111. This was the second time in Ortiz's career that he went the distance, as well as the second time in a row.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Iskenderov |first1=Parviz |title=Vergil Ortiz Jr bests Israil Madrimov by decision to retain interim title |url=https://www.fightmag.com/vergil-ortiz-jr-bests-israil-madrimov-by-decision-to-retain-interim-title/ |work=FIGHTMAG |date=22 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Vergil Ortiz Jr Stays Poised In Slow-Burning Madrimov Matchup To Retain WBC Interim Crown |url=https://ringmagazine.com/en/news/vergil-ortiz-jr-stays-poised-in-slow-burning-madrimov-matchup-to-retain-wbc-interim-crown |work=RingMagazine.com |date=22 February 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

====Ortiz Jr vs. Lubin====
On November 8, 2025, Ortiz Jr defended his interim WBC super welterweight title via 2nd round TKO victory over  [[Erickson Lubin]] in Fort Worth, TX.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-21 |title=V. Ortiz to defend WBC interim title against Lubin |url=https://www.espn.com/boxing/story/_/id/46042190/vergil-ortiz-jr-defend-wbc-interim-title-vs-erickson-lubin |access-date=2025-08-21 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Vergil Ortiz Jr faces Erickson Lubin in Fort Worth, TX in November |url=https://www.fightmag.com/vergil-ortiz-jr-faces-erickson-lubin-in-fort-worth-tx-in-november/ |work=FIGHTMAG |date=21 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Vergil Ortiz Jr vs Erickson Lubin Headlines Nov. 8 DAZN Show in Fort Worth |url=https://bigfightweekend.com/news/vergil-ortiz-jr-vs-erickson-lubin/ |work=bigfightweekend.com |date=21 August 2025}}</ref>

====Ortiz Jr vs. Ennis Negotiations====
As one of the biggest fights in boxing, a bout between Vergil Ortiz Jr and [[Jaron Ennis]] has been in talks for a while, with Ennis previously rejecting proposals to fight Ortiz Jr on undercard fights in Saudi Arabia, not wanting to move up to [[Super Welterweight]] while trying to unify the World Titles at [[Welterweight]]. After Ortiz Jr's bout with Lubin, Ortiz Jr and Ennis officially entered negotiations for a proposed bout at the MGM Grand in March 2026, with Ortiz Jr's promotion Golden Boy Promotions, pulling out of negotiations as both [[Oscar De La Hoya]] and Ortiz Jr's manager Rick Mirigian could not reach an agreement with Ennis's team and Promotion after wanting a 60/40 split in favor of Ortiz Jr.

'''Alus''', an American singer, songwriter, musician, and producer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://thesource.com/2016/10/13/on-the-rise-meet-urban-pop-sensation-alus/|title=On The Rise: Meet Urban Pop Sensation Alus|last=Rose|first=Venus|date=October 13, 2016|website=The Source|access-date=11 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://divagalsdaily.com/diva-chat-latina-singer-alus-channels-the-nineties/|title=DIVA CHAT: Latina Singer Alus Channels the Nineties|date=April 24, 2014|website=DivaGalsDaily|access-date=11 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://okmagazine.com/news/miss-your-90s-divas-listen-to-pop-singer-alus/|title=Miss Your '90s Divas? Listen to Pop Singer Alus!|date=May 8, 2014|website=OK!|access-date=11 August 2019}}</ref>

==Early life==
Alus was born January 1, 1994, in [[New Jersey]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://thesource.com/2015/06/10/alus-reveals-her-new-visual-for-red-hair-dont-care/|title=Alus Reveals Her New Visual For 'Red Hair, Don't Care'|last=Rathon|first=Rocko|date=June 10, 2015|website=The Source|access-date=11 August 2019}}</ref> Her grandmother's music had been a childhood influence, who was a renowned musician in the Violinaires, a group of violinists that performs with [[Frank Sinatra]]'s The [[Rat Pack]]. Alus at a very young age, started performing on stage in musicals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vibe.com/2013/12/meet-alus-the-singer-destined-to-bring-back-90s-styled-music|title=Meet Alus, The Singer Destined to Bring Back 90's Styled Music|date=December 30, 2013|website=Vibe|access-date=11 August 2019}}</ref> When she was eleven years old, she started her classical vocal training in opera from a [[Curtis Institute of Music]] instructor and also received formal classical piano lessons. She is also a [[self-taught]] guitarist.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.blogtalkradio.com/reginaldford/2013/12/19/lotl-welcomes-gifted-singersongwriter--alus-debuts-new-hit-song-relapse|title=LOTL Welcomes gifted singer-songwriter – ALUS . Debuts new hit song ' Relapse|website=BlogTalkRadio|date=December 19, 2013 |access-date=11 August 2019}}</ref>

==Career==
Alus's first release that gained traction was "Ordinary Girl".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/entertainment/music/2014/11/must-hear_nj_urban_pop_singer_alus.html|title=Must-hear N.J.: Urban pop singer Alus makes splash on hip-hop radio and beyond|last=Olivier|first=Bobby|date=November 12, 2014|website=The Star-Ledger|access-date=11 August 2019}}</ref> Released independently with much success on New York Radio, she gained the attention of music veterans [[Steve Rifkind]] and [[Russell Simmons]]. After teaming up with their [[Samsung]] sponsored label All Def Digital, Alus released the official music video that came out on the label's YouTube channel.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wonkysensitive.blogspot.com/2019/07/alus-fck-nudes-send-me-your-playlist.html|title=Alus – F*ck Nudes, Send Me Your Playlist|date=July 12, 2019|website=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://getyourbuzzup.com/2018/04/09/alus-aladdin-video/|title=ALUS debuts her "Aladdin" video and channels the storied princess in a modern day twist @alusofficial|last=Blitz|date=April 9, 2018|website=Get Your Buzz Up|access-date=11 August 2019}}</ref>

Alus records herself in her at home studio, releasing mash-ups and [[Cover (music)|covers]] on her YouTube channel. She released them into monthly albums called the "''Bedroom Covers''" series. Her mashup video of [[XXXTentacion]]’s "[[SAD!]]" and [[The Weeknd]]’s "[[Call Out My Name]]" received over 1 million views. Alus was reposted by [[Nicki Minaj]] twice on her Instagram page after gaining attention from her remix of "[[Megatron (song)|Megatron]]" and mashup of "[[No Frauds]]", "[[Changed It]]", and "[[Regret in Your Tears]]".

Alus sang the national anthem at [[Madison Square Garden]] on many occasions including for the televised sold-out [[Canelo Álvarez|Canelo]] vs. [[Rocky Fielding|Rocky]] boxing match in 2018.

In 2020, Alus released a new song every week in a series entitled "52 Shades of Alus" amassing over one million plays across streaming platforms.

In June 2021, Alus released “Wig!” featuring [[Cakes da Killa]] with sampled vocals from [[Canada's Drag Race]] Lemon in honor of [[Gay pride|Pride Month]]. [[Paper (magazine)|Paper Magazine]] premiered the music video release calling it “a perfect ‘feeling yourself’ bop.”<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.papermag.com/alus-cakes-da-killa-wig-2653385089.html?rebelltitem=4#rebelltitem4|title=Alus and Cakes Da Killer Are Snatching Wigs|last=Moen|first=Matt|date=June 15, 2021|website=Paper Magazine|access-date=28 June 2021}}</ref>

In 2022, Alus independently released "Money Dance" with over 1.5 million views on YouTube.<ref>{{Citation |title=Alus - Money Dance (Official Video) | date=March 18, 2022 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Ng4qyO15hM |access-date=2024-01-04 |language=en}}</ref>

Alus partnered with producer [[Rich Harrison]] to release "Lock In" in August 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-04 |title=Pop Sensation Alus Debuts Infectious New Single "Lock In," Produced By Grammy Award Winner Rich Harrison |url=https://apnews.com/press-release/ein-presswire-newsmatics/music-beyonce-knowles-pop-music-mary-j-blige-grammy-awards-56f181552c720d5188fffcc6f65b5b88 |access-date=2024-01-04 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>

In 2024, she collaborated with [[Dr. Dre]] and [[Snoop Dogg]] on the track “[[Outta Da Blue]]”.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}}

== Personal life ==
Alus is [[Puerto Rican people|Puerto Rican]] on her mother’s side, and [[Russia]]n and [[Austrians|Austrian]] on her father’s. She is an advocate for [[animal rights]], serving as an ambassador for the [[ASPCA]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theboweryelectric.com/event/1728775-alus-fake-frank-northmen-new-york/|title=Alus, Fake Frank, NorthmeN – Tickets – Bowery Electric – New York, NY – July 16th, 2018|website=Bowery Electric {{!}} New York, NY|access-date=11 August 2019|archive-date=August 11, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190811121301/https://www.theboweryelectric.com/event/1728775-alus-fake-frank-northmen-new-york/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Khaneshia Smith Black''' ({{née|'''Smith'''}}),<ref name="FAMU">{{cite web|url=http://www.thefamuanonline.com/2017/03/27/famu-grad-breaks-boundaries/|last=Lofton|first=Jamari|title=FAMU grad breaks down boundaries|work=The FAMUAN|access-date=July 3, 2023|date=March 27, 2017}}</ref> (born May 6, 1985) known professionally as '''KJ Smith''', is an American actress, known for her role as Andrea "Andi" Barnes in the comedy-drama, [[Sistas (TV series)|''Sistas'']].

== Early life ==
Smith was born on May 6, 1985, in [[Tallahassee, Florida]].<ref name="People2020">{{cite web |last1=Tracy |first1=Brianne |date=July 23, 2020 |title=Sistas' KJ Smith Says She Was 'Nervous' to Return to Set amid COVID-19 but Is 'Happy to Be Back' |url=https://people.com/tv/sistas-kj-smith-returning-to-set-amid-coronavirus-emotional-roller-coaster/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200725102624/https://people.com/tv/sistas-kj-smith-returning-to-set-amid-coronavirus-emotional-roller-coaster/ |archive-date=July 25, 2020 |access-date=January 5, 2021 |website=People |language=EN}}</ref> She was a cheerleader and softball player in high school.<ref name=tvg>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/kj-smith/bio/3030362320/|title=KJ Smith|website=TVGuide.com}}</ref> She studied [[Business marketing|Business Marketing]] at [[Florida State University]], where she earned her bachelor's degree and later went on to work in corporate America. Smith later went back to further her education at [[Florida A&M University]], where she studied [[journalism]].<ref name="FAMU"/>

== Career ==
Smith began her acting career in 2009 with appearing in short films and small parts in television comedies include ''[[Conan (talk show)|Conan]]'', ''[[Real Husbands of Hollywood]]'', ''[[Jimmy Kimmel Live!]]'' and ''[[Comedy Bang! Bang! (TV series)|Comedy Bang! Bang!]]''. She also guest-starred in a number of sitcoms such as ''[[Survivor's Remorse]]'', ''[[Mann & Wife]]'', ''[[It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia]]'' and ''[[Black-ish]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brockington |first=Ariana |title=There Are So Many Celebs In 'blackAF' |url=https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/2020/04/9685376/blackaf-netflix-series-cast-celebrity-cameos |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=www.refinery29.com |date=October 2, 2019 |language=en}}</ref> She played secondary role in the 2015 made-for-television movie ''[[Whitney (2015 film)|Whitney]]'' and the following year had a recurring role in the Oprah Winfrey Network drama series, ''[[Queen Sugar]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tallahassee native KJ Smith finds her niche in Hollywood – Capital Outlook |url=http://capitaloutlook.com/site/tallahassee-native-kj-smith-finds-her-niche-in-hollywood/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190621202401/http://capitaloutlook.com/site/tallahassee-native-kj-smith-finds-her-niche-in-hollywood/ |archive-date=June 21, 2019}}</ref>
[[File:KJ Smith 2016.jpg|thumb|Smith in 2016]]
In 2017, Smith had a recurring role during the first season of the CW comedy-drama series, [[Dynasty (2017 TV series)|''Dynasty'']],<ref>{{Cite web |last=TV |first=AfterBuzz |date=2021-11-20 |title=Our EXCLUSIVE Interview with KJ Smith from Dynasty - CW Weekly |url=https://www.afterbuzztv.com/our-exclusive-interview-with-kj-smith-from-dynasty-cw-weekly/ |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=AfterBuzz TV |language=en-US}}</ref> and guest-starred on ''[[Being Mary Jane]]'', ''[[Saints & Sinners (2016 TV series)|Saints & Sinners]]'' and ''[[Ozark (TV series)|Ozark]]''. In 2018, she co-starred in the web drama series, ''[[Giants (web series)|Giants]]'' produced by [[Issa Rae]]. Smith also made guest appearances on ''[[NCIS: Los Angeles]]'', ''[[The Fosters (American TV series)|The Fosters]]'', ''[[Lethal Weapon (TV series)|Lethal Weapon]]'', ''[[Fuller House (TV series)|Fuller House]]'', ''[[Family Reunion (TV series)|Family Reunion]]'', ''[[All Rise (TV series)|All Rise]]'' and ''[[blackAF]]''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Hough |first=Quinn |date=2020-04-19 |title=Every Celebrity Cameo in #blackAF Season 1 |url=https://screenrant.com/black-af-season-1-celebrity-cameos/ |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=ScreenRant |language=en}}</ref> From 2015 to 2018, she had a recurring role on Bounce TV sitcom [[Family Time (TV series)|''Family Time'']] and in 2019 had a recurring role in short-lived ABC legal drama, [[The Fix (2019 TV series)|''The Fix'']],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |date=August 29, 2018 |title=''The Fix'' Casts KJ Smith; Chivonne Michelle Joins ''Jett'' |url=https://deadline.com/2018/08/the-fix-casts-kj-smith-chivonne-michelle-jett-1202454078/ |access-date=September 9, 2019 |website=Deadline Hollywood}}</ref> In 2019, she co-starred in the comedy film ''[[A Madea Family Funeral]]'' and the following year appeared in psychological thriller ''[[Fatal Affair]]'' for Netflix.<ref>{{cite web |last=N'Duka |first=Amanda |date=November 6, 2019 |title=Stephen Lang Joins 'Death in Texas'; KJ Smith Cast In 'Fatal Affair'; Oliver Cooper In 'Ghostbusters' |url=https://deadline.com/2019/11/stephen-lang-death-in-texas-kj-smith-fatal-affair-oliver-cooper-ghostbusters-1202778268/ |access-date=July 3, 2020 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Lawrence |first=Gregory |date=July 1, 2020 |title=The Trailer for Netflix's 'Fatal Affair' Delivers Cheesy Domestic Thriller Realness |url=https://collider.com/fatal-affair-netflix-trailer-nia-long-omar-epps/ |access-date=July 3, 2020 |work=Collider}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Scott |first=A. O. |date=2019-03-01 |title=Review: 'A Madea Family Funeral' Is No Cause for Tears |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/03/01/movies/a-madea-family-funeral-review.html |access-date=2023-03-08 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Smith also played the lead role in the drama film ''The Available Wife'' (2020).<ref>{{Cite web |last=N'Duka |first=Amanda |date=April 24, 2019 |title=Poorna Jagannathan, Nikohl Boosheri to Topline ''Alia{{'s}} Birth''; KJ Smith, Roger Guenveur Smith Co-Star in ''The Available Wife'' |url=https://deadline.com/2019/04/poorna-jagannathan-nikohl-boosheri-alias-birth-kj-smith-roger-guenveur-smith-the-available-wife-1202600835/ |access-date=September 9, 2019 |website=Deadline Hollywood}}</ref>

From 2019 to 2021, Smith starred in the BET family drama series, [[The Family Business (American TV series)|''The Family Business'']]. In 2019 she landed her breakthrough role as Andrea "Andi" Barnes in the BET comedy-drama series, [[Sistas (TV series)|''Sistas'']] opposite [[Ebony Obsidian]], [[Novi Brown]] and Mignon Von.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Throne |first=Will |date=August 1, 2019 |title=Tyler Perry Comedy ''Sistas'' Ordered at BET |url=https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/tyler-perry-comedy-sistas-bet-1203287967/ |access-date=September 9, 2019 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |date=August 1, 2019 |title=BET Greenlights Tyler Perry Drama Series ''Sistas'', Sets Main cast |url=https://deadline.com/2019/08/bet-tyler-perry-drama-series-sistas-cast-1202658271/ |access-date=September 9, 2019 |website=Deadline Hollywood}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Holmes |first=Martin |title='Tyler Perry's Sistas': BET Renews Show For Fourth Season |url=https://www.tvinsider.com/1019043/tyler-perrys-sistas-bet-renews-show-for-fourth-season/ |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=TV Insider |date=October 21, 2021 |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2022, she also had a recurring role in season two of the ''Power'' prequel series, ''[[Power Book III: Raising Kanan]]'', on [[Starz|STARZ]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |date=2021-10-05 |title='Power Book III: Raising Kanan': KJ Smith Joins Prequel Series As Recurring |url=https://deadline.com/2021/10/power-book-iii-raising-kanan-kj-smith-prequel-series-recurring-1234845526/ |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Toby |first=Mekeisha Madden |date=2021-10-06 |title=Power Book III: Raising Kanan Adds Sistas' KJ Smith to Season 2 Cast |url=https://www.tvline.com/casting-news/kj-smith-power-book-iii-raising-kanan-season-2-cast-palomar-1234728859/ |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=TVLine |language=en-US}}</ref>

'Sistas' Stars KJ Smith And Skyh Alvester Black Are Engaged |url=https://www.bet.com/article/8tdgn5/kj-smith-skyh-black-engaged |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228215346/https://www.bet.com/article/8tdgn5/kj-smith-skyh-black-engaged |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 28, 2021 |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=BET |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-12-26 |title='Sistas' Stars KJ Smith And Skyh Alvester Black Engaged Over Christmas! |url=https://hellobeautiful.com/3541740/k-j-smith-and-skyh-alvester-black-engaged-for-christmas/ |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=HelloBeautiful |language=en-US}}</ref> In May 2025, Smith and Black announced that they were expecting their first child.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 12, 2025 |title=KJ Smith and Skyh Black Expecting Their First Child |url=https://www.3music.tv/section/news/article/kj-smith-and-skyh-black-expecting-their-first-child-together-2025-05-12 |website=3music.tv}}</ref> In August 2025, Smith and Black revealed to ''[[People (magazine)|People]]'' that they moved from Los Angeles to [[Stone Mountain, Georgia]] to be closer to their families because both their families are on the East Coast. Their 10,348 sq. ft. property was built in 1976 which consists of five bedrooms, seven bathrooms, an indoor pool, a theater, bar, and gym.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.com/kj-smith-and-skyh-black-have-left-l-a-and-relocated-to-atlanta-see-their-new-home-exclusive-11789091|title=Pregnant KJ Smith and Skyh Black Have Left L.A. for the South — See Their Stunning New Home (Exclusive)|website=[[People (magazine)|People]]|first=Erin|last=Clements|date=August 14, 2025|access-date=August 15, 2025}}</ref> On October 23, 2025, they welcomed their first daughter.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 23, 2025 |title=KJ Smith and Skyh Black Welcome Their First Baby Together and Reveal the Unexpected Way Tyler Perry Was Involved (Exclusive) |url=https://people.com/kj-smith-and-skyh-black-welcome-their-first-baby-together-exclusive-11835198 |website=people.com}}</ref>

'''John Michael Finley''' (born August 10, 1988) is an American actor and singer. He is known for portraying [[Bart Millard]] in the 2018 film ''[[I Can Only Imagine (film)|I Can Only Imagine]]''. He has appeared on [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]], in London’s [[West End theatre|West End]], in the Australian production of ''[[The Book of Mormon (musical)|The Book of Mormon]]'', and in numerous Chicago-area theatres. He is a member of the [[Actors' Equity Association]].<ref name="playbill">{{cite web |title=J. Michael Finley (Performer) |url=https://playbill.com/person/j-michael-finley |website=Playbill |access-date=2025-11-24}}</ref><ref name="marriott">{{cite web |title=J. Michael Finley Biography |url=https://www.marriotttheatre.com/artists/j-michael-finley |website=Marriott Theatre |access-date=2025-11-24}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Finley was born in [[Jonesboro, Arkansas]], and raised in [[Lebanon, Missouri]]. He began singing and acting in junior high school and performed in school and community theatre. He later studied musical theatre at the Chicago College of Performing Arts at [[Roosevelt University]], earning a BFA.<ref name="roosevelt">{{cite web |title=CCPA: J. Michael Finley |url=https://blogs.roosevelt.edu/review/2018/06/21/ccpa-michaelfinley/ |website=Roosevelt University Review |date=2018-06-21 |access-date=2025-11-24}}</ref><ref name="imdbbio">{{cite web |title=John Michael Finley - Biography |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm8722479/bio/ |website=IMDb |access-date=2025-11-24}}</ref>

==Career==
===Early Chicago theatre===
Finley launched his professional career in Chicago, performing in productions at the [[Lyric Opera of Chicago]], [[Paramount Theatre (Aurora, Illinois)|Paramount Theatre]], [[Marriott Theatre]], [[Drury Lane Theatre (Illinois)|Drury Lane Theatre]], [[Writers Theatre|Writers' Theatre]], [[Court Theatre (Chicago)|Court Theatre]], and the Mercury Theatre.<ref name="marriott" /> His early roles included parts in ''Carousel'', ''Camelot'', ''Sweeney Todd'', ''Grease'', ''Hair'', ''James Joyce's The Dead'', and ''A Little Night Music''. <ref name="marriott" />

===Broadway, West End, and international stage===
Finley moved to [[New York City]] in 2015. He made his Broadway debut in the ensemble of ''[[Les Misérables]]'', where he understudied the role of [[Jean Valjean]].<ref name="playbill" />

He later joined the Broadway company of ''[[The Book of Mormon (musical)|The Book of Mormon]]'' as the standby for Elder Cunningham. His performance with the production led to West End and Australian engagements in the same role.<ref name="broadwayworld">{{cite web |title=J. Michael Finley Credits |url=https://www.broadwayworld.com/people/J-Michael-Finley/ |website=BroadwayWorld |access-date=2025-11-24}}</ref><ref name="playbill" />

===Film===
Finley gained widespread recognition for his film debut portraying Bart Millard in the 2018 biographical drama ''[[I Can Only Imagine (film)|I Can Only Imagine]]'', which earned notable box office results for its budget.<ref name="variety">{{cite web |last=McNary |first=Dave |title='I Can Only Imagine' Soars With $17.1 Million Opening |url=https://variety.com/2018/film/box-office/christian-movie-i-can-only-imagine-box-office-1202729700/ |website=Variety |date=2018-03-18 |access-date=2025-11-24}}</ref><ref name="thr">{{cite web |last=Rubin |first=Rebecca |title=Box Office: 'I Can Only Imagine' Revives Faith-Based Genre |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/i-can-imagine-revives-faith-based-genre-at-box-office-1095373/ |website=The Hollywood Reporter |date=2018-03-20 |access-date=2025-11-24}}</ref>

He reprised the role in ''[[I Can Only Imagine 2]]'', released February 20, 2026, with Dennis Quaid and Trace Adkins returning.<ref name="churchleaders">{{cite web |title=John Michael Finley Is 'Really Excited' To Reprise His Role as Bart Millard in 'I Can Only Imagine 2' |url=https://churchleaders.com/news/509899-john-michael-finley-excited-bart-millard-i-can-only-imagine-2.html |website=ChurchLeaders |date=2025-04-17 |access-date=2025-11-24}}</ref>

Finley has also appeared in other faith-based and historical films, including:

* ''Faith of Angels'' (2024), portraying John Skinner, a man whose knowledge of a mine aids in rescuing a lost child.<ref name="churchleaders" />
* ''Love, Courage and the Battle of Bushy Run'' (2024), in which he portrayed Captain John Graham.<ref name="bushyrun">{{cite web |title=Love, Courage and the Battle of Bushy Run Cast |url=https://triblive.com/local/westmoreland/feature-film-love-courage-battle-of-bushy-run/ |website=TribLive |access-date=2025-11-24}}</ref>

===Other work===
Finley has discussed themes of faith, loss, and community in interviews related to his film work, particularly ''Faith of Angels''. <ref name="churchleaders" />

==Personal life==
Finley married Elizabeth Doran on December 2, 2017. He has a baritone singing voice and is a fan of the [[St. Louis Cardinals]]. He is also a member of the [[Actors' Equity Association]].<ref name="marriott" />

'''Daniel Nwosu Jr.''' (born March 22, 1994), professionally known by his [[stage name]] '''Dax''' (often stylized in [[all caps]]), is a Nigerian-Canadian and American<ref>Source: @thatsdax on X https://x.com/thatsdax/status/1432457656942292998</ref><ref>Source: @thatsdax on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdDLaC-tZAj/?stkn=MWE3YjlxZXloZGVqOA==</ref> singer and rapper.<ref>{{Cite web|last=II|first=C. Vernon Coleman|title=Dax's Pitch for 2020 XXL Freshman|url=https://www.xxlmag.com/dax-pitch-2020-xxl-freshman/|access-date=2021-10-14|website=XXL Mag|date=30 March 2020|language=en|archive-date=2021-11-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211102124659/https://www.xxlmag.com/dax-pitch-2020-xxl-freshman/|url-status=live}}</ref> He has recorded three albums, ''Pain Paints Paintings'' (2021), ''From a Man's Perspective'' (2024) and ''Anger Management'' (2026). He has achieved certifications in Canada and the United States for his singles "[[Dear God (Dax song)|Dear God]]", "[[Dear Alcohol]]" and "[[To Be a Man]]."

==Early life and education==
Daniel Nwosu Jr. was born on March 22, 1994, to immigrant [[Nigerian]] parents, in [[St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador|St. John's]], [[Newfoundland and Labrador]]. Nwosu grew up in [[Ottawa]]. He attended [[Casper College]] in [[Casper, Wyoming]], during the 2013–2014 school year, where he played on the [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] Thunderbirds basketball team. He later transferred to play Division I basketball for the [[Montana Grizzlies]] during the 2014–15 season. He then attended [[Newman University, Wichita|Newman University]], where he played guard for the [[Newman Jets]] basketball team. Finally, he was introduced into his long standing friend, Avery Park, who later aided him in his music career.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dax |title=Dax |url=https://daxofficial.com/ |access-date=2026-08-04 |website=Dax |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://newmanjets.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2197|title=Daniel Nwosu Jr. - Men's Basketball|website=Newman University Athletics|language=en|access-date=2019-02-14|archive-date=2016-06-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160620153351/http://newmanjets.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2197|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=How Nigerian-Canadian rapper Dax went from shooting hoops to selling records |url=https://rollingout.com/2019/11/08/nigerian-canadian-rapper-dax-went-from-shooting-hoops-to-selling-records/ |website=Rolling Out |access-date=4 January 2022 |date=8 November 2019 |archive-date=25 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200725062250/https://rollingout.com/2019/11/08/nigerian-canadian-rapper-dax-went-from-shooting-hoops-to-selling-records/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

He initially wrote poetry and was a motivational speaker prior to pursuing a rap career. During his time at Newman University, he worked as a janitor, a job where he says that he was able to develop his poetry and rap skills during downtime.<ref name="kansas">{{Cite web|title=Janitor, musician, basketball star, Newman's Daniel Nwosu Jr. does it all|url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/state-college-sports/article133958499.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180824065801/https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/state-college-sports/article133958499.html|archive-date=2018-08-24|access-date=2019-02-14|website=kansas|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vladtv.com/article/251661/dax-i-was-a-night-janitor-for-25-years-its-the-best-job-for-new-rappers?page=2|title=EXCLUSIVE: Dax: I was a Night Janitor for 2.5 Years, it's The Best Job for New Rappers|website=VladTV|language=en|access-date=2019-06-13|archive-date=2021-06-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624104317/https://www.vladtv.com/article/251661/dax-i-was-a-night-janitor-for-25-years-its-the-best-job-for-new-rappers?page=2|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Artistry==
===Style and influence===
Initially, Dax did not take rap seriously because of his interest in basketball but there was a phase where he grew up listening to [[Tupac]]. He stated that, he was never really a hip-hop enthusiast but he started listening when [[Drake (musician)|Drake]] took over the scene. Dax has also cited artists like [[50 Cent]] and [[Lil Wayne]]. He compares his style to artists such as [[Tech N9ne]], [[Eminem]], and Hopsin.<ref name="XXL" />
Despite his commercial success, Nwosu's musical style has frequently been the subject of internet memes and criticism within the hip-hop community.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Rise of 'Coworker Rap' in Modern Hip-Hop Culture |url=https://hotnewhiphop.com |publisher=HotNewHipHop |date=May 12, 2025 |access-date=July 14, 2026}}</ref> Detractors often label his style as "coworker rap" or "burger music," terms used by online music commentators to describe a hyper-literal, over-the-top, or generic lyrical delivery.<ref>{{cite web |title=Why the Internet Clowns Dax's Lyrical Style |url=https://complex.com |publisher=Complex |date=October 24, 2025 |access-date=July 14, 2026}}</ref> Nwosu has frequently acknowledged the criticism, leaning into the memes on social media to drive user engagement, even earning the [[nickname]] "CEO of Burger Music".<ref>{{cite web |title=How Dax Turned 'Burger Music' Into Social Media Engagement |url=https://xxlmag.com |publisher=XXL Mag |date=March 3, 2026 |access-date=July 14, 2026}}</ref>

==Feuds==
===KSI===
On November 18, 2018, [[KSI]] appeared on the ''What's Good?'' Podcast, where he called out various internet rappers. In the interview KSI said both [[Quadeca]] and Dax were worse than him at rapping. Quadeca went on to post a full diss track against him on November 23, 2018, called "Insecure". Shortly after, Dax also responded with his own diss track, which was a remix of Eminem's diss track toward [[Machine Gun Kelly (musician)|Machine Gun Kelly]], "[[Killshot (song)|Killshot]]". KSI then responded to Dax and Quadeca's track with a reaction video, also accompanied by a diss track called "Ares".{{Citation needed|date=July 2024}}

He challenged Dax to a private boxing match, with Dax accepting but repeatedly delaying it. Dax’s childhood friend and person in charge of Hebrew translation of his songs, Arjun Muramalla, defended Dax saying the fight would be unfair. He then later appeared on Deji's diss track "Unforgivable" against KSI.<ref>{{cite web |title=KSI confirms next Youtube boxing fight and opponent - and fans love it |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/boxing/ksi-confirms-next-youtube-boxing-14052197 |website=Mirror |language=en |date=25 February 2019 |access-date=15 January 2022 |archive-date=15 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220115062807/https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/boxing/ksi-confirms-next-youtube-boxing-14052197 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=KSI and rapper Dax arrange boxing match during heated argument |url=https://www.dexerto.com/entertainment/ksi-rapper-dax-arrange-boxing-match-during-heated-argument-395718/ |publisher=Dexerto |language=en |date=24 February 2019 |access-date=15 January 2022 |archive-date=15 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220115034717/https://www.dexerto.com/entertainment/ksi-rapper-dax-arrange-boxing-match-during-heated-argument-395718/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Tory Lanez===
On January 24, 2019, [[Tory Lanez]] claimed through a tweet that he is the "best rapper alive".<ref>{{cite web |title=Tory Lanez Tweets Then Deletes Apology For Saying He Was The Best Rapper Alive |url=https://hiphopdx.com/news/id.55333/title.tory-lanez-tweets-then-deletes-apology-for-saying-he-was-the-best-rapper-alive |website=HipHopDX |date=7 April 2020 |access-date=15 January 2022 |archive-date=15 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220115062810/https://hiphopdx.com/news/id.55333/title.tory-lanez-tweets-then-deletes-apology-for-saying-he-was-the-best-rapper-alive |url-status=live }}</ref> Dax responded by posting a video on [[YouTube]], featuring a diss track titled "I'm Not Joyner Or Don Q" aimed at him.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tory Lanez Runs Up On Dax Following Diss Record: "Apologize, Bro" |url=https://hiphopdx.com/news/id.50251/title.tory-lanez-runs-up-on-dax-following-diss-record-apologize-bro |website=HipHopDX |access-date=10 February 2019 |date=10 February 2019 |archive-date=11 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190211003040/https://hiphopdx.com/news/id.50251/title.tory-lanez-runs-up-on-dax-following-diss-record-apologize-bro |url-status=live }}</ref> Lanez posted a video on Instagram in response in which he pressures Dax to apologize for the diss track. Dax addressed the situation in interviews with [[DJ Akademiks]], ''[[Logan Paul|Impaulsive]]'', and ''[[Adam22|No Jumper]]'', saying that apologizing was the right thing to do because he did not want a fight to break out.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2019/02/dax-talks-tory-lanez-demanding-an-apology|title=Canadian Rapper Dax Talks About Tory Lanez Pulling Up and Demanding Apology|website=Complex|language=en|access-date=2019-02-14|archive-date=2019-02-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190213023743/https://www.complex.com/music/2019/02/dax-talks-tory-lanez-demanding-an-apology|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Magalí Sesé i Lara''' (born 28 July 1991), known professionally as '''Magalí Sare''', is a [[Catalans|Catalan]] singer and multi-instrumentalist, born into a family of musicians.<ref name="Aniversari">{{cite web |url=https://www.enderrock.cat/noticia/26542/28-juliol-avui-aniversari-magali-sare |title=28 de juliol: Avui és l'aniversari de Magalí Sare |website=[[Enderrock]] |access-date=6 July 2024 |language=ca}}</ref> She obtained the professional degree in transverse flute and lyrical singing at the Conservatori Municipal de Sabadell, where she also studied piano and percussion. At the age of nineteen, she began a higher degree in classical flute at the [[Conservatori Superior de Música del Liceu|Liceu Conservatory of Music]] but completed only two years, deciding to focus on modern music and jazz instead.<ref>{{cite web |title=Magalí Sare: "Compondre em va servir per sentir-me lliure després d'una relació d'abús psicològic" |url=https://www.enderrock.cat/noticia/18234/magali/sare/compondre/em/va/servir/sentir-me/lliure/despr/relacio/abus/psicologic |website=[[Enderrock]] |access-date=24 April 2021 |language=ca}}</ref>

== Musical career ==
In 2012, Sare joined the vocal ''[[a cappella]]'' group [[Quartet Mèlt]] as the soprano voice, performing across Catalonia and Europe. With the group, she released two albums: ''Maletes'' (2016) and ''Xarrampim!'' (2017). Quartet Mèlt gained wide recognition after winning the third season (2015) of the TV3 show ''[[Oh Happy Day]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Quartet Mèlt guanya la tercera edició d'{{'}}Oh Happy Day' |url=https://www.ara.cat/media/quartet-melt-tercera-happy-day_1_1508441.html |date=29 November 2015 |access-date=24 April 2021 |first=Núria |last=Juanico}}</ref>

In 2017, she graduated in jazz singing from the Liceu Conservatory, receiving the department's extraordinary award. During her studies, she formed a duo with guitarist Sebastià Gris, with whom she won two awards: the first prize in Jazz from the Juventudes Musicales de España competition (2018),<ref>{{cite web |title=Els ex-alumnes del Centre Superior Magalí Sare i Sebastià Gris guanyen la primera edició de la Modalitat de Jazz del Concurso Juventudes Musicales |url=https://www.conservatoriliceu.es/noticies/superior/jme-concurs-jazz-premi-sare-gris/ |access-date=24 April 2021 |language=es}}</ref> and the first international prize at the Suns Europe competition for minority languages (2019).

In April 2018, she self-released her first solo album, ''Cançons d'amor i dimonis'' (''Songs of Love and Demons''). That same year she collaborated with [[Clara Peya Rigolfas|Clara Peya]] on the album ''Estómac'', while continuing to perform with Quartet Mèlt until 2021, when she was permanently replaced by Carolina Alabau (who had occasionally substituted for her since 2019).<ref name="quisom">{{cite web |url=http://www.quartetmelt.com/qui-som |title=Qui Som |website=Quartet Mèlt |access-date=6 July 2024 |language=ca}}</ref>

In 2019, Sare was nominated as an emerging talent at the Premis Alícia of the Acadèmia Catalana de la Música, and as breakthrough artist at the Premis ARC. That same year, the poem ''Desplegar-se'' by Sònia Moya, set to music by Sare, was among the five best musical adaptations of the year at the Terra i Cultura contest, receiving a special mention from [[Lluís Llach]].

Since then, Sare has participated in several musical projects, notably two duos: one with guitarist Sebastià Gris, with whom she released ''A Boy and a Girl'' (2020),<ref>{{cite web |title=Magalí Sare i Sebastià Gris: "Qualsevol música que per un segon no ens deixi indiferents, ens ajuda a estar més desperts" |url=https://www.enderrock.cat/noticia/20583/magali-sare-sebastia-gris-qualsevol-musica-segon-no-deixi-indiferents-ajuda-estar-mes-desperts |website=[[Enderrock]] |access-date=24 April 2021 |language=ca}}</ref> and another with New York-based double bassist Manel Fortià. In addition to performing, Sare teaches modern and jazz singing and combo at the [[Taller de Músics]]’ higher education program.

'''Suzuko Ogino''', ({{Langx|ja|荻野 鈴子}};<ref>{{Cite web |title=第２７回参議院議員通常選挙結果調（速報） |url=https://www.soumu.go.jp/main_content/001021472.pdf#page=89 |access-date=2025-07-22 |publisher=総務省 |format=PDF |archive-date=2025-07-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250726220500/https://www.soumu.go.jp/main_content/001021472.pdf#page=89 |url-status=live }}</ref> born 31 January 1994) known by her stage name '''Uryu Hirano''' ({{Lang|ja|平野 雨龍}}) and '''Suzuko Hirano''' ({{Lang|ja|平野 鈴子}}) before 2021, is a Japanese right-wing politician, political activist, and former model. She is the representative of the social organization "Uryu-kai".<ref name=":0" />

Hirano came to public attention following the 2019 Hong Kong pro-democracy movement and has been described as Japan's leading figure opposing the [[2019 Hong Kong extradition bill|Extradition Bill to China]], Taiwanese media occasionally referring to Hirano as the "Anti-Extradition Goddess."<ref name="ltn">{{Cite web |date=2019-08-21 |title=「日本反送中第一人」 和服模特兒IG粉絲1小時暴增3倍 |url=https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/world/breakingnews/2890817 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903083024/https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/world/breakingnews/2890817 |archive-date=2019-09-03 |access-date=2019-09-06 |website=[[:zh:自由電子報|自由電子報]] |language=zh-TW}}</ref> She has been active in advocating for the protection of Uyghur human rights and a review of Japan's immigration policies toward Chinese nationals. Her activities have been reported in media of both Taiwan and Hong Kong.<ref name="ltn" />

Hirano ran as an independent candidate from the Tokyo constituency in the [[2025 Japanese House of Councillors election]], becoming the youngest candidate in the race under an anti-immigrant campaign focusing on strengthening restrictions on Chinese immigration and deepening relations with Taiwan and Hong Kong.<ref>{{Cite web |last=黃信維（コウ・シンイ） |title=独占インタビュー》中国人からの妨害にも屈せず――「反送中」第一人者・平野雨龍氏、日台注目の2025参院選に最年少で挑む {{!}} 黃信維（コウ・シンイ） {{!}} ニュース |url=https://japan.storm.mg/articles/1052849 |access-date=2025-11-04 |website=japan.storm.mg |language=ja}}</ref> Although did not reach the vote threshold for being elected, she received 235,411 votes, placing 14th out of 32 candidates and the highest among all independent candidates.<ref name=":0" />

== Political activism ==
Hirano had visited Hong Kong several times before the [[Anti-Extradition Bill Movement|2019 anti-extradition bill protests]] began, and claims to have many friends there. <ref name="japanforward">{{Cite web |date=2019-07-05 |title=なぜ、私は日本で香港を支援するのか |url=https://japan-forward.com/japanese/%E3%81%AA%E3%81%9C%E3%80%81%E7%A7%81%E3%81%AF%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC%E3%81%A7%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF%E3%82%92%E6%94%AF%E6%8F%B4%E3%81%99%E3%82%8B%E3%81%AE%E3%81%8B/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190915020537/http://japan-forward.com/japanese/%E3%81%AA%E3%81%9C%E3%80%81%E7%A7%81%E3%81%AF%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC%E3%81%A7%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF%E3%82%92%E6%94%AF%E6%8F%B4%E3%81%99%E3%82%8B%E3%81%AE%E3%81%8B/ |archive-date=2019-09-15 |access-date=2019-09-06 |website=JAPAN Forward |language=ja}}</ref><ref name="stand">{{Cite web |date=2019-07-07 |title=日模東京每周辦反送中遊行　至《逃犯條例》撤回為止 |url=https://thestandnews.com/politics/%E6%97%A5%E6%A8%A1%E6%9D%B1%E4%BA%AC%E6%AF%8F%E5%91%A8%E8%BE%A6%E5%8F%8D%E9%80%81%E4%B8%AD%E9%81%8A%E8%A1%8C-%E8%87%B3-%E9%80%83%E7%8A%AF%E6%A2%9D%E4%BE%8B-%E6%92%A4%E5%9B%9E%E7%82%BA%E6%AD%A2/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190814212459/https://thestandnews.com/politics/%E6%97%A5%E6%A8%A1%E6%9D%B1%E4%BA%AC%E6%AF%8F%E5%91%A8%E8%BE%A6%E5%8F%8D%E9%80%81%E4%B8%AD%E9%81%8A%E8%A1%8C-%E8%87%B3-%E9%80%83%E7%8A%AF%E6%A2%9D%E4%BE%8B-%E6%92%A4%E5%9B%9E%E7%82%BA%E6%AD%A2/ |archive-date=2019-08-14 |access-date=2019-09-06 |website=[[:zh:立場新聞|立場新聞]] |language=zh-HK}}</ref><ref name="mpweekly">{{Cite web |date=2019-08-26 |title=「反送中」陰霾 日人重新了解香港命運共同體 |url=https://www.mpweekly.com/culture/%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC-%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC%E5%AA%92%E9%AB%94-%E5%8F%8D%E9%80%81%E4%B8%AD-118806 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306081500/https://www.mpweekly.com/culture/%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC-%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC%E5%AA%92%E9%AB%94-%E5%8F%8D%E9%80%81%E4%B8%AD-118806 |archive-date=2021-03-06 |access-date=2019-09-06 |website=[[:zh:明報周刊|明報周刊]] |language=zh-HK}}</ref> Through [[Twitter]] and other social media platforms, Hirano learned about the ongoing protests and, after watching activist [[Agnes Chow]] explain the 2019 extradition bill on television, she decided to start protesting. At the age of 25 Hirano joined the "Emergency Action to Protect Hong Kong’s Freedom and Democracy" rally in Shibuya on 13 June 2019 — her first-ever participation in a demonstration. The next day, upon learning that another protest was being held six hours later in Nagoya, she left her work, took the [[Tokaido Shinkansen|Tōkaidō Shinkansen]] from Tokyo to [[Kanayama Station (Aichi)|Kanayama]] station and gave a speech at the rally in front of the station. The translated version of her speech was later uploaded online and viewed over 400,000 times. Hirano stated that if the amendment were passed, "Hong Kong would no longer be Hong Kong," expressing concern that the [[Chinese Communist Party]] might expand its influence over Taiwan, East Asia, and even as far as [[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]] and Tokyo.<ref name="mpweekly" /><ref name="japanforward" /><ref name="apple">{{Cite web |date=2019-08-08 |title=蘋人誌： 與港人同行 日模活出武士道 平野鈴子 |url=https://hk.news.appledaily.com/local/daily/article/20190808/20744989 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20190907015146/https://hk.news.appledaily.com/local/daily/article/20190808/20744989 |archive-date=2019-09-07 |access-date=2019-09-06 |website=[[:zh:香港蘋果日報|香港蘋果日報]] |language=zh-HK}}</ref>

Hirano organized her first demonstration against the extradition bill on 29 June 2019 in Tokyo.<ref name="japanforward"/> She declared that she would hold weekly "Solidarity Actions to Defend Hong Kong with the World" every Saturday, marching from [[Hibiya Park]] to [[Tokyo Station]]. Hirano started declining modelling jobs to focus on activism and produced banners at her own expense. Participation numbers were often smaller than expected, leading her to lament Japan's general indifference toward politics. Nonetheless, Hirano stated that she would never regret standing with Hong Kong.<ref name="apple"/><ref name="japantimes">{{Cite web |last=Takahashi |first=Ryusei |date=2019-08-26 |title=Japan conspicuously silent as protests and violent crackdown roil Hong Kong |url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2019/08/26/national/japan-conspicuously-silent-protests-violent-crackdown-roil-hong-kong/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190914023021/https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2019/08/26/national/japan-conspicuously-silent-protests-violent-crackdown-roil-hong-kong/ |archive-date=2019-09-14 |access-date=2019-09-06 |website=[[:zh:日本時報|日本時報]]（網上版） |language=en}}</ref><ref name="stand"/><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-07-06 |title=我願意為了守護香港而死！日本女模自發辦集會「撐」香港 |url=https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/world/breakingnews/2844555 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190820043615/https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/world/breakingnews/2844555 |archive-date=2019-08-20 |access-date=2019-09-06 |website=自由電子報 |language=zh-TW}}</ref>Hirano also voiced anger toward mainland Chinese who erased the slogan "[[Liberate Hong Kong, revolution of our times|Liberate Hong Kong, Revolution of Our Times]]" written on [[Ema (Shinto)|ema]] plaques at shrines or discouraged others from supporting the protests.<ref name="ltn2">{{Cite web |title=神社求「光復香港」遭改「一個中國」 日模特兒：不要破壞日本 - 國際 - 自由時報電子報 |url=https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/world/breakingnews/2892839 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903095818/https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/world/breakingnews/2892839 |archive-date=2019-09-03 |access-date=2019-09-06 |website=自由電子報 |language=zh-TW}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-08-25 |title=香港之路 21萬人牽手響應 |url=https://hk.news.appledaily.com/local/daily/article/20190825/20755599 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190827091525/https://hk.news.appledaily.com/local/daily/article/20190825/20755599 |archive-date=2019-08-27 |access-date=2019-09-06 |website=香港蘋果日報 |language=zh-HK}}</ref>

In addition to organising marches, Hirano used social media to raise awareness about the situation in Hong Kong, conducted fundraising campaigns, and participated in the "#eye4hk" challenge by posting a selfie covering her right eye.<ref name="ltn2"/><ref name="ltn"/> On 11 August 2019, Hirano attended [[Comiket]], where she and several international students cosplayed Hong Kong protesters in helmets and masks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-08-12 |title=【逃犯條例】平野鈴子Cosplay香港示威者 頭盔口罩寫滿標語 |url=https://www.hk01.com/%E5%8D%B3%E6%99%82%E5%A8%9B%E6%A8%82/362564/%E9%80%83%E7%8A%AF%E6%A2%9D%E4%BE%8B-%E5%B9%B3%E9%87%8E%E9%88%B4%E5%AD%90cosplay%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF%E7%A4%BA%E5%A8%81%E8%80%85-%E9%A0%AD%E7%9B%94%E5%8F%A3%E7%BD%A9%E5%AF%AB%E6%BB%BF%E6%A8%99%E8%AA%9E |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903083034/https://www.hk01.com/%E5%8D%B3%E6%99%82%E5%A8%9B%E6%A8%82/362564/%E9%80%83%E7%8A%AF%E6%A2%9D%E4%BE%8B-%E5%B9%B3%E9%87%8E%E9%88%B4%E5%AD%90cosplay%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF%E7%A4%BA%E5%A8%81%E8%80%85-%E9%A0%AD%E7%9B%94%E5%8F%A3%E7%BD%A9%E5%AF%AB%E6%BB%BF%E6%A8%99%E8%AA%9E |archive-date=2019-09-03 |access-date=2019-09-06 |website=[[:zh:香港01|香港01]] |language=zh-HK}}</ref> On 6 September, Hirano attended a Hong Kong press event, where she criticised the police for an indiscriminate arrest of a Japanese national on [[2019 Prince Edward station attack|Prince Edward station on 31 August]] and denying consular contact. She also said she had been at Prince Edward station on 3 September and later learned on Twitter that a 21-year-old protester had suffered a cervical spine injury, which enraged her deeply. Declaring her resolve to "fight thoroughly alongside the people of Hong Kong," Hirano said she had been frequently attacked and even threatened with death by [[50 Cent Party|Wumao]] netizens.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-09-06 |title=眾新聞 {{!}} 民間記者會：五大訴求只撤修例是「糖衣毒藥」 籲美通過《香港人權與民主法案》 == Elections ==
Hirano ran as an independent candidate in [[2025 Japanese House of Councillors election|July 2025 House of Councillors election]] from the [[Tokyo at-large district|Tokyo constituency]], campaigning under the slogan "A [[Heisei era|Heisei]]-born woman for the [[National Diet]]!". Her campaign has been described as having an anti-immigrant stance without any concrete policy packages.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chai |first1=Peter |title=Beyond Sanseito: Anti-Immigrant Rhetoric in Japan’s Upper House Election |url=https://thediplomat.com/2025/08/beyond-sanseito-anti-immigrant-rhetoric-in-japans-upper-house-election/ |website=The Diplomat |access-date=2026-07-10}}</ref> Although she did not reach the vote count threshold to get elected,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-21 |title=東京選挙区、無所属の平野雨龍氏が落選…政治団体代表 |url=https://www.yomiuri.co.jp/election/sangiin/20250721-OYT1T50001/ |access-date=2025-11-05 |website=読売新聞オンライン |language=ja |archive-date=2025-07-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250720235739/https://www.yomiuri.co.jp/election/sangiin/20250721-OYT1T50001/ |url-status=live }}</ref> she received 235,411 votes, placing 14th out of 32 candidates, getting the highest vote count among all independent candidates without party backing.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=平野雨龍（ヒラノウリュウ）｜政治家情報｜選挙ドットコム |url=https://go2senkyo.com/seijika/193460 |access-date=2025-11-05 |website=選挙ドットコム |language=ja |archive-date=2025-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250918230812/https://go2senkyo.com/seijika/193460 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the [[2026 Japanese general election]] she ran for a seat in the [[House of Representatives (Japan)|House of Representatives]] in the [[Ōita 3rd district]], challenging former Foreign Minister [[Takeshi Iwaya]]. She ended up third with 14.5% of the vote.
