'''Melania Dalla Costa''' (born 25 February 1988) is an Italian actress, screenwriter, film producer, and activist.

== Biography ==
Melania Dalla Costa was born in [[Marostica]], Province of [[Vicenza]], on 25 February 1988. A former [[athlete]], she practised cross-country skiing competitively for ten years.

She was the creative producer of Magic Fair, a global sales and production company based in the United States, Italy, and France.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://forbes.it/2020/09/01/melania-dalla-costa-da-attrice-a-producer-e-imprenditrice/|title=Da attrice a producer e imprenditrice|website=Forbes Italia|date=2020-09-01}}</ref>

She began her artistic training in 2011 at Elf Teatro (Raul Manso), continued in 2012 at Spazio Gedeone (Paolo Olgiati). In 2013 she studied acting and diction at Centro Teatro Attivo (Nicoletta Ramorino). In 2014 she trained at Conservatorio Teatrale Diotaiuti (Giovanni Battista Diotaiuti), and from 2015 to 2018 with Ivana Chubbuck, Bernard Hiller and Michael Margotta.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://rebelmanagement.it/melania-it/|title=Melania - IT}}</ref> Between 2024 and 2025 she began screen-combat (stunt) training for actors.

Between 2018 and 2019, the press referred to her as “the muse of [[Giovanni Gastel]]”; she was the sole subject of his exhibition ''Cattura'', displayed in Milan on Via della Spiga.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.artribune.com/arti-visive/fotografia/2018/12/intervista-a-melania-della-costa-la-musa-di-giovanni-gastel-protagonista-della-mostra-cattura/|title=Intervista a Melania Dalla Costa|website=Artribune|date=2018-12-15}}</ref> In 2019 she was testimonial for the United Nations [[United Nations Interregional Crime and Justice Research Institute|UNICRI]] campaign against violence against women.

In 2020 she appeared in ''Dream Ladies'' with [[Lily Collins]], [[Fan Bingbing]], [[Alice Braga]], [[Enikő Mihalik]], [[Leomie Anderson]] and [[Róisín Murphy]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lofficielitalia.com/digital-issues/l-officiel-italia-n-35-dream-ladies|title=L'Officiel Italia N°35 in versione digitale sfogliabile|website=www.lofficielitalia.com}}</ref>

''Grazia Arabia'' featured her among the international women who inspire the magazine.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.spaghettimag.it/2021/11/30/in-conversation-with-melania-dalla-costa/|title=In conversation with Melania Dalla Costa|website=Spaghettimag|date=2021-11-30}}</ref>

In 2021 she appeared on the January cover of ''Harper’s Bazaar Serbia''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://models.com/work/harpers-bazaar-serbia-harpers-bazaar-serbia-january-2021-cover|title=Harper's Bazaar Serbia January 2021 Cover (Harper's Bazaar Serbia)|website=MODELS.com}}</ref> and on the April covers of ''Glamour Mexico'' and ''Glamour Latin America''. The same year she was testimonial for the [[Mille Miglia]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vanityfair.it/vanityfood/food-news/2021/06/22/melania-dalla-costa-eleganza-e-sparkling-life-alla-gara-piu-bella-del-mondo/amp|title=Melania Dalla Costa alla Mille Miglia|author=Anna Mazzotti|date=2021-06-22|work=Vanity Fair}}</ref>

In 2022 she appeared on the July cover of ''[[Harper's Bazaar|Harper’s Bazaar]] Bulgaria''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/Cf8k3CJKcKs/|title=Instagram|website=www.instagram.com}}</ref>
That December she became the global face of the [[Maserati]] Grecale Modena campaign, distributed by [[Condé Nast]] International across ''British Vogue'', ''Vogue'' America,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vogue.com/sponsored/article/italian-french-actress-melania-dalla-costa-takes-us-on-an-extraordinary-tour-of-milan|title=Italian French Actress Melania Dalla Costa takes us on an extraordinary tour of Milan|date=November 28, 2022|website=Vogue}}</ref> ''Vogue Singapore'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://vogue.sg/melania-dalla-costa-milan-maserati-grecale/|title=Actress Melania Dalla Costa takes Vogue on an awe-inspiring city tour through Milan|first=Vogue|last=Singapore|date=December 3, 2022}}</ref> ''Vogue Philippines'', ''Vogue Korea'', ''British GQ'', ''[[GQ]] US'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gq.com/sponsored/story/actor-melania-dalla-costa-guides-gq-through-the-milan-spots-that-make-every-day-exceptional|title=Actor Melania Dalla Costa Guides GQ Through the Milan Spots That Make Every Day Exceptional|date=November 30, 2022|website=GQ}}</ref> ''GQ Italy'', ''GQ Germany'', ''GQ China'', ''GQ Taiwan'' and ''GQ Japan''.

She was godmother of the [[Carnival of Venice|Venice Carnival]] 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://carnevale.venezia.it/news/2023/melania-dalla-costa-madrina-carnevale-di-venezia-2023/|title=Melania Dalla Costa è la Madrina del Carnevale di Venezia 2023|first=Carnevale di|last=Venezia|date=February 20, 2023}}</ref>
Since January 2023 she has been part of the “Bvlgari Family,” following a collaboration that began in 2018.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://models.com/people/melania-dalla-costa|title=Melania Dalla Costa - Actor|website=MODELS.com}}</ref>
Since 2024 she has collaborated with Christian Dior.<ref name="auto"/>

On 25 January 2025, she was invited by fashion designer Sabyasachi Mukherjee to Mumbai for his 25th-anniversary show; the event was covered by ''[[The Times of India]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/life-style/spotlight/melania-dalla-costa-reflects-on-sabyasachis-25th-anniversary-a-timeless-fashion-experience/articleshow/117684463.cms|title=Melania Dalla Costa in Mumbai|work=The Times of India|access-date=2025-01-30}}</ref>

== Actress ==
Her breakthrough came in 2014 with the TV drama ''[[Un posto al sole]]'', playing Francesca.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vanityfair.it/show/tv/14/05/12/un-posto-al-sole-melania-dalla-costa-intervista-foto|title=Un posto al sole – Interview|work=Vanity Fair|date=2014-05-12}}</ref>

In 2015 she acted in the fashion short film ''Only When I’m Alone I Find Myself and I Often Check If I’m Lost'', wearing [[Antonio Marras]]’s Spring/Summer 2015 collection.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lagazzettadellospettacolo.it/cinema/99870-melania-dalla-costa-venezia79/|title=Melania Dalla Costa tra i volti di Venezia79|first=Alessia|last=Giallonardo|date=September 11, 2022}}</ref>

From 2016 to 2020 she worked in both film and television (''Immaturi'', by Rolando Ravello).

She co-starred with [[Francesca Inaudi]] in ''Stato di ebbrezza'', released on 24 May 2018 and presented at the [[Cannes Film Festival]], playing Beatrice, a drug-addicted and suicidal woman.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.movietele.it/stato-di-ebbrezza-film-luca-biglione-cannes-2018-cinema|title=Stato di ebbrezza di Luca Biglione a Cannes 2018|date=May 10, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.giornalettismo.com/spettacolo/melania-dalla-costa-la-mia-ragazza-interrotta-nel-film-stato-di-ebrezza/|title=Melania Dalla Costa: 'Stato di Ebbrezza', presto al cinema nel ruolo di Beatrice (Intervista)|date=February 20, 2018}}</ref>

On 16 October 2025 she appeared with James Franco in the international feature ''Squali'', directed by Daniele Barbiero, playing Valeria.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tg24.sky.it/spettacolo/cinema/2025/10/16/squali-film|title=Squali – Sky TG24|date=2025-10-16}}</ref>

== Screenwriter ==
She debuted as a screenwriter in 2018 with ''I sogni sospesi''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elle.com/it/showbiz/tv/a28897077/melania-dalla-costa-intervista-venezia-2019/|title=Sul divano del Central Perk (a Venezia 2019) con Melania Dalla Costa per celebrare i 25 anni di Friends|date=September 3, 2019|website=ELLE}}</ref>
The film deals with the traumatic past of a woman victim of sexual abuse.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.giornalealtopiano.it/news.php?cod=13-02-2021-melania-dalla-costa-una-bellezza-canonica-impreziosita-da-modernita-e-intraprendenza|title=Melania Dalla Costa: una bellezza canonica impreziosita da modernità e intraprendenza|first=Michele|last=Berardi|website=www.giornalealtopiano.it}}</ref>

Her subsequent works include: ''Thebes'', ''La Lupa'', ''Medusa'', ''The Golden Blood'', ''The Northern Star'', ''Bonecrackers'' and ''The Magnificent Rebels of Venice''.

== Activism ==
In addition to charity work in Italy and other countries,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.spaghettimag.it/2021/11/30/in-conversation-with-melania-dalla-costa/|title=In conversation with Melania Dalla Costa|first=Anna Chiara Delle|last=Donne|date=November 30, 2021}}</ref> in 2018 she wrote, produced and starred in ''I sogni sospesi'', presented at the [[Venice Film Festival|Venice International Film Festival]].

An activist for women’s rights, she was testimonial in 2019 for the UNICRI campaign against violence against women.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.onuitalia.it/una-campagna-dellunicri-con-melania-dalla-costa-e-dimitri-dimitracacos-per-leliminazione-della-violenza-contro-le-donne/|title=UNICRI campaign – Onu Italia}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.panorama.it/lifestyle/melania-dalla-costa-testimonial-della-campagna-2019-dellunicri-dellonu|title=Melania Dalla Costa testimonial della campagna 2019 dell'Unicri dell'Onu|first=Andrea|last=Soglio|date=November 24, 2019}}</ref>

In 2021 ''[[Marie Claire]]'' (Spain) selected her—with Eva Longoria, Alicia Keys and Isabeli Fontana—for ''Mujeres Empoderadas''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marie-claire.es/planeta-mujer/fotos/mujeres-empoderadas-melania-dalla-costa-611622388588|title=Mujeres Empoderadas – Marie Claire|access-date=2025-12-06|archive-date=2022-12-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201064754/https://www.marie-claire.es/planeta-mujer/fotos/mujeres-empoderadas-melania-dalla-costa-611622388588|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 8 March 2023 she helped realise an artwork by [[Liu Bolin]] dedicated to Iranian women, involving activist Nasibe Shamsaei.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.artribune.com/mostre-evento-arte/liu-bolin-per-liran/|title=Liu Bolin per l'Iran | Artribune|date=March 13, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vogue.it/news/article/liu-bolin-donne-iraniane-nasibe-shamsaei-melania-dalla-costa|title=Melania Dalla Costa ci racconta la mostra per le donne iraniane nel segno di Nasibe Shamsaei|first=Giacomo|last=Aricò|date=March 30, 2023|website=Vogue Italia}}</ref>

Racing Technology in Porsche Carrera Cup France. ==Career== Guibbert began karting at the age of ten, competing until 2023.{{cite web|url=https://www.kartmag.fr/iame-muret-retour-sur-les-masters-gentlemen-kz2-et-ka100/|title=IAME Muret: Retour sur les Masters, Gentlemen, KZ2 et KA100|date=1 March European [[Original Kart|KF2]] Trophy.{{cite web|url=https://www.kartcom.com/en/news/2010/11/08/guibbert-champion-de-france-kf2/|title=Guibbert Champion de France KF2|date=8 November 2010|website=kartcom.com|access-date=13 December 2025|lang=fr}}{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport-xl.de/news/2011/CIK-FIA/Spanien-und-Frankreich-siegen-in-Varennes-2078.html|title=Spanien und Academy]]-centrally run [[2012 French F4 Championship|French F4 Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.kartcom.com/en/news/2011/12/23/guibbert-choisit-la-f4/|title=Guibbert choisit la F4|date=23 December 2011|website=kartcom.com|access-date=13 December 2025|lang=fr}} Starting off the season with a third-place finish at [[Circuit de Lédenon|Lédenon]],{{cite web|url=https://www.kartcom.com/it/news/2012/05/04/guibbert-3eme-a-ledenon/|title=Guibbert, 3ème à Lédenon|date=4 May 2012|website=kartcom.com|access-date=13 December 2025|lang=fr}} Guibbert then scored second-place finishes at [[Circuit du Val de Vienne|Val de Vienne]] and [[Circuit de Nevers Magny-Cours|Magny-Cours]] en route to a fourth-place points finish.{{cite web|url=https://www.kartcom.com/en/news/2012/07/14/f4-magny-cours-baron-toujours-sans-rival/?s=tirman%20simon|title=F4 Magny-Cours: Baron toujours sans rival|date=14 July 2012|website=kartcom.com|access-date=13 December 2025|lang=fr}}{{cite web|url=https://www.midilibre.fr/2014/04/22/sauvian-enzo-17-ans-deja-tout-d-un-grand,851474.php|title=Sauvian : Enzo 17 ans, déjà [[Alméras Frères|Pro GT by Almeras]] for his maiden season in the FFSA GT Championship.{{cite web|url=https://www.midilibre.fr/2013/04/26/enzo-17-ans-affronte-sur-les-circuits-panis-et-villeneuve,686456.php|title=Enzo, Héraultais de 17 ans, sur les circuits avec Panis et Villeneuve|date=26 '''Ramón Bueno Gonzalbo''' (born 7 February 1995), is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]].

== Club career ==
Born in [[Burriana, Castellón|Burriana]], Spain, Bueno represented [[Villarreal CF (youth)|Villareal Juvenil]], and [[Villarreal CF C|Villareal C]] as a youth.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ramón Bueno, un burrianense que triunfa en la Selección Española Sub 17 |url=https://www.elperiodic.com/burriana/ramon-bueno-burrianense-triunfa-seleccion-espanola_143785 |date=2 November 2011|access-date=7 January 2026|website=elperiodic |language=es}}</ref> After impressing in the academy team, ahead of the 2016 season, he joined [[Villareal CF|Villareal]] and was immediately assigned to [[Villarreal CF B|Villareal B]] in [[Segunda División B]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Profil Ramon Bueno Gonzalbo: Pemain Baru Persija, Didikan Villarreal |url=https://onefootball.com/fr/news/profil-ramon-bueno-gonzalbo-pemain-baru-persija-didikan-villarreal-39768247 |date=16 July 2024|access-date=7 January 2026|website=onefootball.com |language=id}}</ref> He was included in Villarreal's first team squad for the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League qualifying]], against [[AS Monaco|Monaco]]. However, he was only on the bench for the first leg and was not included in the squad for the second leg.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Profil Ramon Bueno Gonzalbo: Pemain Baru Persija yang Sempat Perkuat Timnas Spanyol |url=https://sosok.co.id/read/q-27/profil-ramon-bueno-gonzalbo-pemain-baru-persija-yang-sempat-perkuat-timnas-spanyol |date=16 July 2024|access-date=7 January 2026|website=sosok.co.id |language=id}}</ref>

Bueno played in 38 matches in the [[2018–19 Segunda División B|2018–19 season]]. He was even linked with a move to [[UD Almería|Almería]]. However, he remained with Villarreal and played in 22 matches in the [[2019–20 Segunda División B|2019–20 season]] until he was sidelined by injury and unable to play for 17 months.<ref name="bueno">{{Cite web |title=Ramón Bueno, consistencia para el centro del campo del Córdoba CF|url=https://www.eldiadecordoba.es/cordobacf/Ramon-Bueno-consistencia-Cordoba-CF_0_1694532462.html |date=20 June 2022|access-date=7 January 2026|website=www.eldiadecordoba.es |language=es}}</ref> In the [[2021–22 Primera División RFEF|2021–22 season]], he returned to the pitch after suffering a complete tear of the [[anterior cruciate ligament]] and a partial tear of the [[medial collateral ligament]] in his right knee in January 2020. Now recovered from his injury, he has played in 17 matches.<ref name="bueno" />

In June 2022, [[Primera Federación]] side [[Córdoba CF|Córdoba]] announced the signing of Bueno for two-years contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=El Córdoba CF mueve ficha: Ramón Bueno, hasta 2024|url=https://www.eldiadecordoba.es/cordobacf/Cordoba-CF-mueve-Ramon-Bueno_0_1693931223.html |date=18 June 2022|access-date=7 January 2026|website=www.eldiadecordoba.es |language=es}}</ref> Bueno made his club debut on 4 September 2022, replacing [[Javi Flores]] in a 3–0 home win against [[CF Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Un equipo con mayúsculas (3-0)|url=https://www.eldiadecordoba.es/cordobacf/cordoba-cf-fuenlabrada-resultado-partido_0_1717329005.html |date=4 September 2022|access-date=7 January 2026|website=www.eldiadecordoba.es |language=es}}</ref> In 2023, Córdoba has reached an agreement to loan him to [[CF Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]] until the end of the season, with the aim of giving him more playing time. However, he remains under contract with Córdoba for another year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ramón Bueno deja el Córdoba CF y se marcha cedido al Fuenlabrada|url=https://www.eldiadecordoba.es/cordobacf/Ramon-Bueno-Cordoba-CF-Fuenlabrada_0_1762024140.html |date=31 January 2023|access-date=7 January 2026|website=www.eldiadecordoba.es |language=es}}</ref>

In July 2023, Bueno joined [[SD Tarazona|Tarazona]], previously, he left Córdoba in June due to a release clause that allowed the club to terminate the remaining year of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ramón Bueno seguirá en Primera Federación|url=https://cordobadeporte.com/ramon-bueno-seguira-en-primera-federacion/ |date=27 July 2023|access-date=7 January 2026|website=cordobadeporte |language=es}}</ref> He made 21 appearances for Tarazona, without scoring.<ref name="ramon1">{{Cite web |title=El exótico destino de Ramón Bueno: Un ex del Córdoba CF que jugará en Indonesia|url=https://www.eldiadecordoba.es/cordobacf/destino-ramon-bueno-ex-cordoba-cf_0_2001692371.html |date=17 July 2024|access-date=7 January 2026|website=eldiadecordoba |language=es}}</ref>

=== Persija Jakarta ===
On 16 July 2024, Bueno moved abroad for the first time in his career, after agreeing to a year contract with Indonesian [[Liga 1 (Indonesia)|Liga 1]] side [[Persija Jakarta]].<ref name="ramon1" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://persija.id/berita/detail/mari-berjuang-bersama-ramon-bueno |title=MARI BERJUANG BERSAMA, RAMON BUENO!|publisher=persija.id|language=id|date=16 July 2024|access-date=7 January 2026}}</ref> He made his debut abroad five days later, replacing [[Hanif Sjahbandi]] in a 2–1 win over [[Madura United F.C.|Madura United]] in a pre-season [[2024 Indonesia President's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://jatim-timur.tribunnews.com/2024/07/22/ramon-bueno-tampil-menawan-di-laga-debut-bersama-persija-anak-emas-thomas-doll-kena-senggol |title=Ramon Bueno Tampil Menawan di Laga Debut Bersama Persija, Anak Emas Thomas Doll Kena Senggol|publisher=tribunnews|language=id|date=22 July 2024|access-date=7 January 2026}}</ref> And made his first league appearance on 10 August 2024, in a 3–0 won against [[PS Barito Putera|Barito Putera]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tempo.co/sepakbola/hasil-liga-1-persija-jakarta-vs-barito-putera-3-0-gustavo-almeida-borong-ketiga-gol-26977 |title=Hasil Liga 1: Persija Jakarta vs Barito Putera 3-0, Gustavo Almeida Borong Ketiga Gol|publisher=www.tempo.co|language=id|date=10 August 2024|access-date=7 January 2026}}</ref>

'''Roan Curtis''' (born February 1, 1997) is a Canadian actress. She is best known for playing Young Kate in the drama series ''[[Firefly Lane]]'' and Marian Sykes in the teen drama film ''[[Before I Fall (film)|Before I Fall]]''.

==Early life==
Curtis is from [[Vancouver]], British Columbia<ref>{{Cite web|title='Firefly Lane' star Sarah Chalke gets crafty doing voice work from home during COVID|url=https://www.townandcountrytoday.com/lifestyle/firefly-lane-star-sarah-chalke-gets-crafty-doing-voice-work-from-home-during-covid-3356012|access-date=April 5, 2026 |website=[[TownandCountryToday.com]]}}</ref> to entrepeneur Kildare Curtis and Stephanie Butler.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Here's Why Roan Curtis (Young Kate in 'Firefly Lane') Looks So Familiar|url=https://www.purewow.com/entertainment/roan-curtis|access-date=April 5, 2026 |website=purewow.com}}</ref> At the age of 8 she began acting and convinced her parents to sign her with one of Canada's top talent agencies.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Roan Curtis|url=https://www.hallmarkchannel.com/hope-valley-1874/cast/roan-curtis|access-date=April 5, 2026 |website=hallmarkchannel.com}}</ref> She was involved with the theater in her high school. In the 8th grade she played Juliet in ''[[Romeo and Juliet]]'', her first Shakespearan play.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Roan Curtis on Saying Goodbye to 'Firefly Lane' and What Kate Taught Her|url=https://thenerdsofcolor.org/2023/05/13/roan-curtis-on-saying-goodbye-to-firefly-lane-and-what-kate-taught-her/|access-date=April 5, 2026 |website=thenerdsofcolor.org}}</ref>

==Career==
Early on in her career she made appearances in the action series ''[[Supernatural (American TV series)|Supernatural]]'' portraying a demon and in the superhero series ''[[Smallville]]'' portraying a young version of Lily Sullivan played by [[Allison Mack]]. Curtis first recurring role came playing Emma Gilbert in the drama series ''[[Shut Eye]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sarah Chalke and Roan Curtis: Find out who plays Kate and her younger self on Firefly Lane|url=https://www.monstersandcritics.com/tv/sarah-chalke-and-roan-curtis-find-out-who-plays-kate-and-her-younger-self-on-firefly-lane/|access-date=April 5, 2026 |website=monstersandcritics.com}}</ref> Her first big role came playing Sylvia in the crime series ''[[The Magicians (American TV series)|The Magicians]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Interview: Firefly Lane’s Sarah Chalke and Roan Curtis
|url=https://brieftake.com/video-interview-firefly-lane-sarah-chalke-roan-curtis/|website=brieftake.com|access-date=April 5, 2026}}</ref> She played Marian Sykes, one of the lead characters in the teen drama film ''[[Before I Fall (film)|Before I Fall]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Here’s Why Roan Curtis (Young Kate in ‘Firefly Lane’) Looks So Familiar|url=https://www.yahoo.com/lifestyle/why-roan-curtis-young-kate-153300894.html|website=yahoo.com|access-date=April 5, 2026}}</ref> Her biggest role so far has been playing Young Kate in the drama series ''[[Firefly Lane]]'' starring [[Katherine Heigl]] and [[Sarah Chalke]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=‘Firefly Lane’: Ali Skovbye & Roan Curtis To Play Young Tully & Young Kate In Netflix Drama Series|url=https://deadline.com/2019/09/firefly-lane-ali-skovbye-roan-curtis-to-play-young-tully-young-kate-in-netflix-drama-series-1202732516/|access-date=April 5, 2026|website=deadline.com}}</ref> As of 2026 she is currently playing Olivia Quinn in the drama series ''Hope Valley 1874'' starring [[Bethany Joy Lenz]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jill Hennessy, Roan Curtis and Lachlan Quarmby Talk ‘Hope Valley: 1874’|url=https://fangirlish.com/2026/03/28/jill-hennessy-roan-curtis-and-lachlan-quarmby-talk-hope-valley-1874/|access-date=September 1, 2025 |website=fangirlish.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Jill Hennessy, Roan Curtis and Lachlan Quarmby Talk ‘Hope Valley: 1874’|url=https://www.digitaljournal.com/entertainment/jill-hennessy-roan-curtis-and-lachlan-quarmby-discuss-hope-valley-1874/article|access-date=April 5, 2026 |website=digitaljournal.com}}</ref>

'''Alexander MacNicoll''' (born August 1, 1989) is an American actor and producer. He is known for portraying Dr. Van Markus on the [[NBC]] medical drama ''[[Brilliant Minds]]'' (2024–2026) and Luke Holbrook on the [[Netflix]] mystery series ''[[The Society (TV series)|The Society]]'' (2019). He also had a recurring role as Colton on the Amazon comedy-drama ''[[Transparent (TV series)|Transparent]]'' (2014–2019).

==Early life and education==

He was born and raised in Hunterdon County, New Jersey. He discovered acting during his senior year of high school through a television and media class and by making short films in his English class, later switching to a theater major at [[DeSales University]] in Center Valley, Pennsylvania.<ref name="canvasrebel">{{cite web |url=https://canvasrebel.com/meet-alex-macnicoll/ |title=Meet Alex MacNicoll |publisher=CanvasRebel Magazine |date=January 6, 2025}}</ref> After graduating, MacNicoll moved to [[Los Angeles]] in 2013, working multiple jobs simultaneously including as a server, bartender, dog walker, and security guard while pursuing acting.<ref name="canvasrebel" />

==Career==

His on-screen debut came in 2013 with the television series ''Auditions from Hell''. He gained early recognition with a recurring role as Colton on [[Amazon Prime Video]]'s comedy-drama ''[[Transparent (TV series)|Transparent]]'', appearing in five episodes in season two."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2016/10/transparents-alex-macnicoll-miles-oliver-daly-movie-1201842531 |title=Transparent's Alex MacNicoll Joins Oliver Daly Indie Pic 'Miles' |publisher=Deadline |date=October 25, 2016}}</ref>

His early film work included the [[Disney]] sports drama ''[[McFarland, USA]]'' (2015) as Fitz Mitchell, which was his first [[SAG-AFTRA|SAG]] job,<ref name="popcult">{{cite web |url=http://pop-culturalist.com/exclusive-interview-pop-culturalist-chats-with-the-rising-hawks-alex-macnicoll/ |title=Exclusive Interview: Pop Culturalist Chats with The Rising Hawk's Alex MacNicoll |publisher=Pop-Culturalist |date=October 2020}}</ref> the football drama ''[[My All American]]'' (2015) as Mike Campbell, and the science-fiction film ''[[The 5th Wave (film)|The 5th Wave]]'' (2016) as Flintstone. On television, he appeared in episodes of ''[[Criminal Minds]]'', ''[[The Fosters (American TV series)|The Fosters]]'', ''[[Bones (TV series)|Bones]]'', and ''[[Rizzoli & Isles]]'', before landing a recurring role as Peter Standall on Netflix's ''[[13 Reasons Why]]'' (2017–2020). In 2018, he appeared in the science-fiction film ''[[A.X.L.]]'' as Sam Fontaine, a rival motocross racer.<ref>{{cite web |title=A-X-L Film Review: Robot-Dog Tale Is a Bucket of Bolts and Borrowed Ideas |url=https://www.thewrap.com/a-x-l-film-review-alex-neustaedter/ |website=The Wrap}}</ref>

In 2019, MacNicoll was cast as Luke Holbrook, a former high school quarterback in a  relationship with Helena, played by [[Natasha Liu Bordizzo]], in the [[Netflix]] mystery series ''[[The Society (TV series)|The Society]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2018/11/rachel-keller-gideon-adlon-cast-chris-keyser-marc-webb-netflix-ya-drama-series-the-society-1202510209/ |title=Rachel Keller & Gideon Adlon Among 14 Cast In Chris Keyser & Marc Webb's Netflix YA Drama Series 'The Society' |publisher=Deadline |date=November 2018}}</ref> Created by Christopher Keyser and released on May 10, 2019, the series follows teenagers who return from a canceled school trip to find their Connecticut town completely cut off from the outside world. The series was renewed for a second season in July 2019 but was cancelled on August 21, 2020, due to complications arising from the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web |title='The Society,' 'I Am Not Okay With This' Canceled at Netflix |url=https://variety.com/2020/tv/news/the-society-i-am-not-okay-with-this-canceled-netflix-1234743782/ |website=Variety |date=21 August 2020}}</ref>

''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'' reported in 2023 that he had been cast as series regular Dr. Van Markus alongside [[Zachary Quinto]] in the NBC medical drama pilot [[Brilliant Minds]].<ref name="deadlinewolf">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2023/04/zachary-quinto-led-nbc-medical-drama-pilot-wolf-casting-1235332689/ |title=Alex MacNicoll, Spence Moore II, Aury Krebs & Ashleigh LaThrop Board NBC Medical Drama Pilot 'Wolf' |publisher=Deadline |date=April 20, 2023}}</ref> The series inspired by the work of neurologist [[Oliver Sacks]] premiered on [[NBC]] on September 23, 2024. He plays a medical intern diagnosed with [[Mirror-touch synesthesia|Mirror-Touch Synesthesia]], a rare condition causing him to physically experience the sensations of those around him.<ref name="nbcseason2">{{cite web |url=https://www.nbc.com/nbc-insider/brilliant-minds-season-2-cast |title=Meet the New Cast Members of Brilliant Minds |publisher=NBC Insider |date=September 2025}}</ref> To prepare, MacNicoll researched the experience of Joel Salinas, a neurologist at [[NYU Langone Health]] who lives with the condition, telling NBC Insider: "It was just all about reading up on that and learning about his experience and trying to apply it to my own life."<ref name="nbcmirror">{{cite web |url=https://www.nbc.com/nbc-insider/brilliant-minds-alex-macnicoll-dr-van-markus-mirror-touch-interview |title=Brilliant Minds' Alex MacNicoll on Dr. Van's Mirror-Touch: 'It Made Me a Better Person' |publisher=NBC Insider |date=October 2024}}</ref> The series was renewed for a second season, which premiered on September 22, 2025.<ref name="deadlinereturn">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2026/03/brilliant-minds-return-date-season-2-guest-cast-nbc-1236752955/ |title='Brilliant Minds' Sets Return Date For Remaining Season 2 Episodes |publisher=Deadline |date=March 2026}}</ref>

In 2025, ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'' reported his casting in the indie horror film ''Sweetest Day''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2025/04/indie-horror-sweetest-day-cast-filming-wraps-1236368745/ |title=Doree Seay, Alex MacNicoll & Chris Labadie Cast In 'Sweetest Day' |publisher=Deadline |date=April 2025}}</ref> In March 2026, ''Deadline'' reported that he had been cast in ''Change the Prophecy'', a short film from writer and director Lindsay Grossman serving as a television proof-of-concept.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2026/03/taylor-richardson-alex-macnicoll-cast-change-the-prophecy-short-1236758355/ |title=Taylor Richardson & Alex MacNicoll Set For Short 'Change The Prophecy' |publisher=Deadline |date=March 2026}}</ref>

'''Kyle Searles''' (born June 24, 1985) is a former American [[Television actor|television actor.]] Searles is best known for his role as Mac on the long-running family drama series ''[[7th Heaven (TV series)|7th Heaven]]''

==Acting career==
Searles had roles on several television shows in the 2000s, with his first TV credit coming in 2001 as a contestant on the teenage version of [[Survivor (American TV series)]] called [[Moolah Beach]]. Searles first acting credit was a guest role on a 2003 episode of the NBC drama [[American Dreams]]. Searles was cast in [[Desperate Housewives]] as John Rowland in the unaired pilot episode; however, he was later replaced by [[Jesse Metcalfe]] when the pilot episode was reshot, but he was given a minor role in the new pilot.<ref>{{cite web |last1=DeMarco |first1=Patrick |title=10 Things You Probably Never Knew About Desperate Housewives on the Gay-Loved Show's 10th Anniversary |url=https://www.phillymag.com/news/2014/10/03/10-things-probably-never-knew-desperate-housewives-gay-loved-shows-10th-anniversary/ |website=phillymag.com |access-date=25 July 2026 |date=3 October 2014}}</ref>
In 2004 Searles was cast in his best known role as Mac, the best friend and baseball teammate of [[Tyler Hoechlin]] character [[Martin Brewer]] on the [[The WB]]/[[The CW]] family drama [[7th Heaven (TV series)]], appearing in 27 episodes throughout the show's final four seasons, the second most episodes by an actor that was never promoted to main cast status, only behind veteran actor [[Christopher Michael]] who appeared in 45 episodes across the show's 11 seasons as a law enforcement officer.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mac |url=https://www.tvmaze.com/characters/249706/7th-heaven-mac |website=tvmaze.com}}</ref> Searle's second most prominent role was as Jake Kessler, an antagonist on the final season the teen drama [[South of Nowhere]]  the character of Jake Keller was a manipulative, smooth-talking, opportunistic aspiring music manager and boyfriend of [[Eileen April Boylan]] character [[Kyla Woods]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Jake Kessler |url=https://www.tvmaze.com/characters/91172/south-of-nowhere-jake-kessler |website=tvmaze.com}}</ref>  South Nowhere ran from 2005 to 2008 on the teen programming block, [[The N]] on [[Noggin (brand)]] though it was on a small network the show is viewed as cutting edge and ahead of it time especially for having two of the main female characters be in a relationship with each other.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=CURVE |date=2017-03-31 |title=Why South of Nowhere Was the Best Show About Young Queer Women For Its Time - CURVE |url=https://www.curvemag.com/blog/why-south-of-nowhere-was-the-best-show-about-young-queer-women-for-its-time/ |access-date=2026-10-13 |language=en-US}}</ref> Searles had one or two episodes guest spots on   ''[[Malcolm in the Middle]]'', ''[[the George Lopez Show]]'', [[Veronica Mars]] and ''[[Dawson's Creek]]. Searles had a recurring role on the short lived drama series [[Swingtown|Swingtown.]] His career lasted less then a decade within the'' 2000's but even so he built a name for himself mostly for his work on family and teen dramas; his final acting credit was a small guest role on a 2009 episode of [[NCIS (TV series)|NCIS]].

== Hollywood Demons Interview ==
In 2025 Searle's sat down for an interview as a part of an episode of [[Drew Pinsky]] [[Investigation Discovery]] documentary series Hollywood Demons, the topic of the episode was his disgraced 7th Heaven co-star [[Stephen Collins]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nolasco |first1=Stephanie |title='7th Heaven' star Stephen Collins' accuser reveals 'worst part' of hearing his sexual misconduct confession |url=https://www.foxnews.com/entertainment/7th-heaven-star-stephen-collins-accuser-reveals-worst-part-hearing-sexual-misconduct-confession |website=Fox News.com |access-date=19 June 2026 |date=24 March 2025}}</ref> In his interview Searls said he admired Collins during the making of the show, explaining: “He would drive to work in a beautiful [[Toyota Prius]] every single morning when the man was making enough money that he could have been driving up in a [[Bentley]]. He could have been decked-out, dressed in the nines, but he was wearing what [[Jay Leno]] typically wears, with the blue jeans shirt and jeans. I always felt like I want to be like that. I need to model myself after him more." However, Searles later teared up while watching Collins confess in a 2014 interview with [[Katie Couric]] on [[ABC 20/20|ABC’s “20/20.]] to sexual misconduct against three under age girls in 1973, 1982 and 1994  Searles reacted to the admission by saying: “This is the first time that I’ve ever thought that he’s full of shit.”“I have like, a knot in my stomach,” Searle's added. “My whole world changed when I had kids, my whole world view. And certainly my tolerance for this. I think that goes without being said. I just think that maybe I put him up on a professional pedestal a bit too much".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharf |first=Zack |date=2025-03-21 |title=‘7th Heaven’ Actors Listen to Co-Star Stephen Collins’ Sexual Misconduct Confession for the First Time: ‘He Would Be a Dead Man if That Was My Child’ |url=https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/7th-heaven-actors-stephen-collins-sexual-misconduct-1236344754/ |access-date=2026-10-13 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> 

== Personal Life ==
Searles left [[Los Angeles]] and moved to [[McKinney, Texas]] in 2012, where he started a family. Since 2013, he has been working as a realtor, and he joined the Ohlig Group in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kyle Searles Realtor |url=https://www.experience.com/reviews/kyle-3848207}}</ref>Searles dated actress [[Brittany Snow]] from 2003 to 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-10-14 |title=Brittany Snow |url=https://www.bellazon.com/main/topic/6806-brittany-snow/ |access-date=2026-09-28 |website=Bellazon |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Biography ==

'''Luca Carabetta''' (born 10 June 1991) is an Italian politician. From 2018 to 2022, he was a member of the [[Chamber of Deputies (Italy)|Chamber of Deputies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.camera.it/deputati/elenco/18-307500|title=Luca Carabetta|publisher=[[Chamber of Deputies (Italy)|Chamber of Deputies]]|language=it}}</ref> From 2018 to 2020, he served as deputy chairman of the Productive Activities Committee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://parlamento18.openpolis.it/parlamentare/carabetta-luca/925908|title=On. Luca Carabetta|publisher=[[:it:Openpolis|Openpolis]]|language=it}}</ref>

==Biography==
A graduate of the [[Polytechnic University of Turin]] with a degree in Energy Engineering, he has worked as an innovation consultant and project manager. The founder of two startups in the field of new technologies, he also served as a parliamentary assistant for the Five Star Movement during the 17th legislature of the Italian Republic.

In the 2018 general election, he was elected to the Chamber of Deputies as a member of the [[Five Star Movement]] in the Piedmont 1 - 02 multi-member district. In June 2018, he was elected Vice Chair of the Chamber of Deputies’ Committee on Productive Activities.

He served as head of innovation for the Five Star Movement’s “Team of the Future”<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.repubblica.it/politica/2019/12/15/news/5s_di_maio_presenta_i_facilitatori-243563702/|title=5S, Di Maio presenta i facilitatori. "E' il team del futuro"|website=la Repubblica}}</ref> from 2019 to 2021. Since December 2021, he has served as coordinator of the Five Star Movement’s digital transition committee.

In the 2022 general election, he ran as a candidate for the Five Star Movement in the single-member district of Piedmont 1 - 03 (Collegno), where he received 14.59% of the vote and was defeated by Elena Maccanti of the center-right (39.94%) and Davide Gariglio of the center-left (31.20%); he also placed second in the multi-member constituency of Piedmont 1 - 02, but since the list did not win any seats there, he was not reelected.

Since July 2025, he has served as Country Manager of [[Trade Republic]] Italia.<ref>{{Cite web|language=it|author=MF Milano Finanza|url=https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/luca-carabetta-e-il-nuovo-country-manager-per-l-italia-di-trade-republic-202507290927114590|title=Luca Carabetta è il nuovo country manager per l’Italia di Trade Republic  MilanoFinanza News|website=MF Milano Finanza}}</ref>

'''Gabriel Fernando Brisola Amaral Silva''' (born 15 October 1998) better known by his artistic name '''Gaab''', is a Brazilian singer and composer.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Como Gaab passou de "filho do Rodriguinho" a compositor e cantor |url=https://entretenimento.uol.com.br/noticias/redacao/2019/05/30/como-gaab-passou-de-filho-do-rodriguinho-a-compositor-e-cantor.htm |access-date=2019-06-09 |website=entretenimento.uol.com.br |language=pt-br}}</ref> His father is singer [[Rodriguinho (singer)|Rodriguinho]].

== Career ==
Coming from a family of musicians, such as his father [[Rodriguinho (singer)|Rodriguinho]] and uncle Ah! Mr. Dan, Gaab, as a teenager, began to accompany his father on tour as a backing vocalist for his team. He composed his first song when he was just 14 years old, and would send it to [[Thiaguinho (singer)|Thiaguinho]], who liked it and decided to record it for his album ''Hey, Mundo''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rodriguinho relembra como ouviu a primeira música do seu filho: 'Ele mandou direto para o Thiaguinho' |url=http://gshow.globo.com/Musica/noticia/2016/05/rodriguinho-relembra-como-ouviu-primeira-musica-do-seu-filho-ele-mandou-direto-para-o-thiaguinho.html |access-date=2019-03-10 |website=Música |language=pt-br}}</ref> Despite his familiarity with [[pagode]], Gaab sought references in [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]] and [[Pop music|pop]], which led him to signing a contract with GR6 Explode.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-06-04 |title=Gaab conta sobre seu novo DVD, inspirações e projetos futuros |url=http://www.latinosbrasil.com/gaab-conta-sobre-seu-novo-dvd-inspiracoes-e-projetos-futuros/ |access-date=2019-12-20 |website=Latinos Brasil |language=pt-BR}}</ref>

In 2016, he and his friends Negretes and Fabinho, created a band called ''Dinastia'', but the group broke up the same year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=OFuxico |title=Rodriguinho produzindo o filho: 'A ideia é deixar ele feliz' |url=https://www.ofuxico.com.br/noticias-sobre-famosos/rodriguinho-produzindo-o-filho-a-ideia-e-deixar-ele-feliz/2016/01/26-256732.html |access-date=2019-12-20 |website=www.ofuxico.com.br |language=pt-br}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=20 novos músicos que prometem para 2018, segundo o Google |url=https://veja.abril.com.br/entretenimento/20-novos-musicos-que-prometem-para-2018-segundo-o-google/ |access-date=2019-12-20 |website=VEJA |language=pt-BR}}</ref> On 9 September 2016, he released his first album which was self-titled and had a single in "Só Você Não Vê". Guest appearances included his father Rodriguinho and the singers Thomaz Melo and Vilc. On 15 September 2017, he released his second album, ''Melhor Viagem'', which has as singles "Cuidado", "Tô Brisando em Você", "Tem Café", "Positividade", "Vai Passar" and "Melhor Viagem", and has as guest appearances [[MC Hariel]], Lest Gang, and Júnior Lord. This would be followed by the release of his first EP, ''Legado: Músicas Para Brisar'', on 18 December, which he released together with his father. The EP has six tracks mixed in with hits between both of them.

On 27 July 2018, Gaab released his third studio album, titled ''U'', which has as singles "U", "Preservê", "De Uns Dias", and "Sem Pressa". Guest appearances included Rodriguinho, Thomaz, Ana Gabriela, and MC Livinho.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zatz |first=Henry |date=2018-07-27 |title=Ouça: Gaab lança álbum “U” com participação de MC Livinho |url=https://br.nacaodamusica.com/noticias/gaab-album-u/ |access-date=2019-12-20 |website=Nação da Música |language=pt-BR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Vivian Andrade |date=2018-07-29 |title=Gaab lança clipes de seu novo projeto: 'U' |url=http://popnow.com.br/gaab-lanca-clipes-de-seu-novo-projeto-u/ |access-date=2019-12-20 |website=Portal PopNow |language=pt-BR}}</ref> On 4 January 2019, he released his first DVD, titled ''Legado: O Show'', in partnership with his father and Ah! '''Sarah Suphellen''' (born 10 July 1998) is a Norwegian footballer who plays as a centre-back for [[Røa IL]].

==Career==
Hailing from [[Trondheim]] and starting her youth career in [[Nardo FK]], she moved to the dominant team in the city, [[SK Trondheims-Ørn]], in the summer of 2014. She made her first-team debut in March 2015 against Sandviken. She also represented Norway internationally from the U16 category up to the U23 team.<ref name=nff>{{NFF|3581336}}</ref>

At a time when Trondheims-Ørn struggled against relegation from the [[2018 Toppserien]], Suphellen was recruited to reigning Norwegian league champions [[LSK Kvinner FK]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rb.no/lsk-kvinner/sarah-suphellen/hege-riise/i-sommer-var-dette-rett-og-slett-fjernt-for-meg/s/5-43-876307|title=– I sommer var dette rett og slett fjernt for meg|date=13 September 2018|work=Romerikes Blad|language=no|access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref> Suphellen and LSK Kvinner also competed in Europe, reaching the quarter-finals of the [[2018–19 UEFA Women's Champions League knockout phase|2018–19 UEFA Women's Champions League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.vg.no/sport/i/RRzjQW/lsk-kvinner-profil-foran-barcelona-moetet-naa-vet-vi-mer-hva-som-kommer|title=LSK Kvinner-profil foran Barcelona-møtet: – Nå vet vi mer hva som kommer|date=27 March 2019|work=VG|language=no|access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref>

Halfway into 2019, Suphellen moved to [[Røa IL]]. She was not able to play due to a knee injury,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rb.no/plutselig-hovnet-kneet-til-sarah-21-opp-uvanlig-at-spillere-ikke-vet-hvilken-hendelse-som-utloste-skaden/s/5-43-1188299|title=Plutselig hovnet kneet til Sarah (21) opp: – Uvanlig at spillere ikke vet hvilken hendelse som utløste skaden|date=15 November 2019|work=Romerikes Blad|language=no|access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref> but was finally cleared to play her first Røa match in August 2020.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://dynamitegirls.no/nyheter/suphellen-fikk-sin-debut|title=Suphellen fikk sin debut|date=4 August 2020|publisher=Røa IL|language=no|access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref> Røa were relegated to the [[2021 Norwegian First Division (women)|2021 First Division]], but gained re-promotion after that single season. Suphellen now served as the [[captain (association football)|team captain]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.akersposten.no/siri-46-var-gullgenerasjonen-na-er-det-sarahs-tur-26-shit-na-ma-vi-gjore-alt-mye-bedre/s/5-142-198144|title=Siri (46) var gullgenerasjonen. Nå er det Sarahs tur (26)|date=27 September 2024|work=Ullern Avis Akersposten|language=no|access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref> In mid-2024 she extended her contract to the end of 2027.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tv2.no/direkte/0nr51/sportsdognet-live/667ec70cce8e52aa6d803906/roakapteinen-forlenger-til-2027|title=Røa-kapteinen forlenger til 2027|date=28 June 2024|publisher=TV 2|language=no|access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref> She played her 200th [[Toppserien]] game on 15 August 2026.<ref name=nff/>

==Personal life==
Outside of football, Suphellen studied medicine.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.akersposten.no/sarah-26-og-ragne-23-kombinerer-studier-og-jobb-helt-avhengig-av-a-ha-noe-ved-siden-av/s/5-142-199905|title=Sarah (26) og Ragne (23) kombinerer studier og jobb|date=19 October 2024|work=Ullern Avis Akersposten|language=no|access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Martín Yamir Ortega''' (born 20 August 1999) is an Argentine professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Right-back|right-back]] for [[Newell's Old Boys]].

==Career==
===Quilmes===
Ortega came through the youth setup at [[Quilmes Atlético Club|Quilmes]] and made his debut on 28 November in a [[Primera Nacional]] game against [[Club y Biblioteca Ramón Santamarina|Santamarina]], which Quilmes lost 1–0.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quilmes: En este campeonato, Quilmes sigue apostando a los pibes |url=https://www.soloascenso.com.ar/notas/quilmes/en-este-campeonato-quilmes-sigue-apostando-a-los-pibes/154761 |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=www.soloascenso.com.ar |language=es}}</ref> He scored his first professional goal in a 3–1 win against [[Chacarita Juniors]] on 22 June 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-26 |title=Quilmes goleó a Chacarita y sueña con el reducido /// QUILMES AC |url=https://quilmesaclub.org.ar/futbol/noticias/1624712649_quilmes-goleo-a-chacarita-y-suena-con-el-reducido |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=QUILMES AC |language=es-ar}}</ref>

===Tigre===
On 8 July 2022, he signed for [[AFA Liga Profesional de Fútbol|Liga Profesional]] club [[Club Atlético Tigre|Tigre]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2022-07-07 |title=Martín Ortega pasará a Tigre {{!}} El Dia |url=https://www.eldia.com/nota/2022-7-7-8-17-0-martin-ortega-pasara-a-tigre-quilmes |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=El Día de La Plata |language=es-AR}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club on 26 February 2024 in a [[2024 Copa de la Liga Profesional|Copa de la Liga Profesional]] game against [[Club Atlético Vélez Sarsfield|Vélez Sarsfield]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Martín Ortega se la jugó y anotó el primer gol de Tigre en la Copa de la Liga ante Vélez |url=https://www.espn.com.ar/futbol/argentina/nota/_/id/13291818/martin-ortega-anoto-primer-gol-de-tigre-en-la-copa-de-la-liga |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=www.espn.com.ar}}</ref> After infrequent appearances in his first two seasons, he established himself in the team in 2024, with his performances leading him to being linked to European clubs including [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] and [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-08-23 |title=Martín Ortega es el candidato favorito como recambio de Juanlu |url=https://as.com/futbol/martin-ortega-es-el-candidato-favorito-como-recambio-de-juanlu-n/ |access-date=2026-09-11 |work=Diario AS |language=es}}</ref> With his contract set to expire on 31 December 2025, he was unable to agree an extension and was left out of the team while it went unresolved.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garcia |first=Luciano |date=2025-10-02 |title=La salida de Ortega de Tigre: los detalles del conflicto, por qué se dio y qué dicen las partes |url=https://www.quepasaweb.com.ar/la-salida-de-ortega-de-tigre-detalles-del-conflicto-y-que-dicen-las-partes-lgd1025/ |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=Que Pasa Web |language=es}}</ref> He left at the end of the year and was rumoured to be on [[Racing Club de Avellaneda|Racing Club]]'s shortlist to replace [[Facundo Mura]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-15 |title=El jugador que Racing tiene en carpeta - TyC Sports |url=https://www.tycsports.com/racing-club/racing-tiene-a-martin-ortega-en-carpeta-para-reemplazar-a-facundo-mura-id704013.html |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=www.tycsports.com |language=es-AR}}</ref>

===Newell's Old Boys===
After several months without a club, he joined [[Newell's Old Boys]] on 3 March 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-03 |title=Bombazo en el Parque: Martín Ortega es refuerzo de Newell’s |url=https://www.redboing.com/bombazo-en-el-parque-martin-ortega-es-refuerzo-de-newells/ |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=RedBoing |language=es-AR}}</ref> He made his debut on 17 March in a 5–0 defeat against [[Club Atlético Lanús|Lanús]], in which he gave away a penalty after a handball.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2026-03-17 |title=Estudiantes de La Plata le ganó 2-1 a Gimnasia de Mendoza y es nuevo escolta en la Zona A del Apertura |url=https://www.infobae.com/deportes/2026/03/17/tres-partidos-cerraran-la-actividad-de-la-fecha-11-del-torneo-apertura-hora-tv-y-formaciones/ |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=infobae |language=es-AR}}</ref>
